speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत संजय ॥
iast:
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata saṃjaya ||
english: On the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus, my sons and the sons of Pandu have gathered, eager to fight. What did they do, Sanjaya?

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ।
आचार्यमुपसंगम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
iast:
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā |
ācāryamupasaṃgamya rājā vacanamabravīt ||
english: But when King Duryodhana saw the Pandava army drawn up in battle order, he went up to his teacher and spoke these words.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् ।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
iast:
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||
english: Teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by your gifted student, the son of Drupada.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि ।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
iast:
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi |
yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ ||
english: Here are heroes, mighty archers equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, a great chariot-warrior;

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥
iast:
dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān |
purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ ||
english: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, a bull among men;

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
iast:
yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān |
saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ ||
english: the bold Yudhamanyu and the valiant Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra and the sons of Draupadi: all of them great chariot-warriors.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
iast:
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama |
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te ||
english: Now hear, best of the twice-born, about the most distinguished among us, the leaders of my army. I name them for you so that you know them.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिंजयः ।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥
iast:
bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiṃjayaḥ |
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca ||
english: You yourself, Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa, victorious in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and also the son of Somadatta.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
iast:
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ |
nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ ||
english: And many other heroes are ready to give up their lives for my sake, armed with many kinds of weapons, all of them skilled in war.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
iast:
aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
paryāptaṃ tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam ||
english: Our army, guarded by Bhishma, is not enough, while their army, guarded by Bhima, is enough.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
iast:
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ |
bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||
english: So all of you, standing in your assigned places at every point of the formation, must protect Bhishma above all.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
iast:
tasya saṃjanayanharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān ||
english: Then, to cheer him, the mighty Bhishma, eldest of the Kurus and their grandfather, roared like a lion and blew his conch.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः ।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
iast:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ |
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat ||
english: Then conches and kettledrums, tabors, drums and horns all sounded at once, and the noise was tremendous.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
iast:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau |
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||
english: Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their great chariot yoked to white horses, blew their divine conches.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
iast:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ ||
english: Krishna blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, doer of fearsome deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
iast:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau ||
english: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
iast:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ |
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ ||
english: The king of Kashi, a superb archer, and Shikhandi, a great chariot-warrior; Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki;

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते ।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
iast:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate |
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak ||
english: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O king, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra: on every side, each blew his own conch.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥
iast:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan ||
english: That tumultuous roar, echoing through sky and earth, tore apart the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥
iast:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrānkapidhvajaḥ |
pravṛtte śastrasaṃpāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
english: Then Arjuna, whose banner bears a monkey, saw Dhritarashtra's sons drawn up in order. As the weapons were about to clash, the son of Pandu raised his bow

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
iast:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate |
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta ||
english: and spoke these words to Krishna, O king: "Krishna, halt my chariot between the two armies,

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यावदेतान्निरिक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् ।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे ॥
iast:
yāvadetānnirikṣe'haṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān |
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasmin raṇasamudyame ||
english: so that I can look at those standing here eager to fight, and see whom I must fight in this coming battle.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
iast:
yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṃ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ ||
english: I want to see those who have gathered here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra in battle."

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
iast:
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam ||
english: Spoken to in this way by Arjuna, O king, Krishna drew up that finest of chariots between the two armies,

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् ।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
iast:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti ||
english: in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the rulers of the earth, and said: "Son of Pritha, look at these Kurus gathered together."

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् ।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥
iast:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān |
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṝnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā ||
english: There the son of Pritha saw them standing: fathers and grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends,

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
iast:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi |
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān ||
english: fathers-in-law and companions, in both armies. Seeing all these relatives standing there, the son of Kunti

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् ।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
iast:
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt |
dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam ||
english: was overcome with deep compassion, and in despair he said: "Krishna, seeing my own people standing here, eager to fight,

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
iast:
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate |
na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ ||
english: My bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin is burning. I cannot stand steady, and my mind seems to be reeling.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
iast:
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
english: Krishna, I see bad omens, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
iast:
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā ||
english: Krishna, I do not want victory, or a kingdom, or pleasures. What use to us is a kingdom, or enjoyment, or even life?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
iast:
yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca ||
english: The very people for whose sake we wanted a kingdom, enjoyment and pleasures stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth:

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
iast:
etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana |
api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte ||
english: I do not want to kill them, Krishna, even if they kill me, not even to rule the three worlds, let alone this earth.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन ।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
iast:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana |
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ ||
english: What joy could we have from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, Krishna? Only sin would come to us from killing these aggressors.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
iast:
tasmānnārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān |
svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava ||
english: So it is not right for us to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own relatives. How could we be happy after killing our own people, Krishna?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
iast:
yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam ||
english: Even if they, their minds overcome by greed, do not see the wrong in destroying a family, or the sin in betraying friends,

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
iast:
kathaṃ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana ||
english: why should we not know to turn back from this sin, Krishna, when we can clearly see the wrong in destroying a family?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः ।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
iast:
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo'bhibhavatyuta ||
english: When a family is destroyed, its timeless family traditions perish; and when that dharma is lost, lawlessness overtakes the whole family.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः ।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसंकरः ॥
iast:
adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ |
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ ||
english: When lawlessness prevails, Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt; and when the women are corrupt, the varnas become mixed.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
संकरो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च ।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
iast:
saṃkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ ||
english: This mixing drags the family and those who destroyed it down to hell, for their ancestors fall, deprived of their offerings of rice and water.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसंकरकारकैः ।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
iast:
doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṃkarakārakaiḥ |
utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ ||
english: Through these wrongs of those who destroy families, which cause the mixing of varnas, the timeless duties of caste and family are wiped out.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन ।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥
iast:
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana |
narake'niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma ||
english: We have heard, Krishna, that people whose family traditions have been destroyed live in hell for an endless time.
codex_problem: “For an endless time” overstates अनियतं, which means an indefinite or unfixed period, not necessarily an endless one.
codex_sanskrit_says: We have heard, Janardana, that people whose family duties have been destroyed dwell in hell for an indefinite period.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
iast:
aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ ||
english: Alas! We are set on committing a great sin, ready to kill our own people out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
iast:
yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
english: It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle while I stood unarmed and did not resist."

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
iast:
evamuktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat |
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ ||
english: Having said this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of his chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed with grief.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
iast:
kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna ||
english: Arjuna, where has this faintness of heart come from at this critical moment? It is not the way of a noble person; it does not lead to heaven, and it brings disgrace.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
iast:
klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate |
kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa ||
english: Son of Pritha, do not give in to unmanliness; it does not suit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and stand up, scorcher of enemies.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रति योत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
iast:
kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana |
iṣubhiḥ prati yotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana ||
english: Krishna, how can I fight back with arrows in battle against Bhishma and Drona? They deserve my reverence, destroyer of enemies.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
iast:
gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyamapīha loke |
hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān ||
english: It would be better to live in this world even by begging than to kill these noble teachers. If I killed my teachers, however much they seek gain, I would enjoy here only pleasures stained with blood.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम- स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
iast:
na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāma- ste'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ ||
english: Nor do we know which is better for us: that we defeat them, or that they defeat us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us; if we killed them, we would not even wish to live.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद् यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
iast:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām |
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam ||
english: I see nothing that could drive away this grief that dries up my senses, even if I won an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth, or even lordship over the gods.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
iast:
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa |
na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha ||
english: Having spoken this way to Krishna, Arjuna said to him, "I will not fight," O king, and fell silent.
codex_problem: “O king” does not render the Sanskrit epithet परन्तप, “scorcher of enemies.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha said to Govinda, “I will not fight,” O scorcher of enemies, and then fell silent.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
iast:
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase |
gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
english: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
iast:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ |
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param ||
english: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; and none of us will ever cease to exist in the future.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
english: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes into another body. A steady person is not confused by this.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥
iast:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati ||
english: Know that what pervades all this is indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
iast:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
anāśino'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata ||
english: These bodies of the eternal, indestructible, immeasurable embodied self are said to come to an end. So fight, Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
iast:
ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate ||
english: Whoever thinks this self is a killer, and whoever thinks it is killed, neither of them understands. It does not kill, and it is not killed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācinnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
english: The self is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will never stop being. Unborn, eternal, constant and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
iast:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam |
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam ||
english: Son of Pritha, how can a person who knows this self to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging kill anyone, or cause anyone to be killed?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
iast:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi |
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇānyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||
english: As a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self throws away worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
iast:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||
english: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
iast:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca |
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ ||
english: It cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, stable, unmoving and timeless.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते ।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate |
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi ||
english: It is called unmanifest, beyond thought and unchanging. So, knowing it to be like this, you should not grieve.

why_listed: safety flags: death, under18_hold; random sample
speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
english: And even if you think of the self as constantly being born and constantly dying, even then, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve like this.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
english: Death is certain for whoever is born, and birth is certain for whoever dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
iast:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata |
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā ||
english: Beings are unmanifest at their beginning, manifest in their middle, Arjuna, and unmanifest again at their end. What is there to lament in that?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
english: The self that dwells in every body is eternal and can never be killed, Arjuna. So you should not grieve for any being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
iast:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi |
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate ||
english: And looking at your own duty, you should not waver; for a warrior, there is nothing better than a war fought for what is right.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
iast:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam |
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam ||
english: Fortunate are the warriors, son of Pritha, who find a war like this, come of its own accord: an open door to heaven.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi ||
english: But if you do not fight this righteous battle, you will give up your duty and your honour, and you will incur sin.

why_listed: safety flags: war, death, under18_hold, distress_gentle
speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām |
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate ||
english: People will tell of your disgrace for ever, and for someone who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam ||
english: The great warriors will think you pulled back from battle out of fear, and those who once thought highly of you will think little of you.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ||
english: Your enemies will say many things that should never be said, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ ||
english: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, resolved to fight.

why_listed: safety flags: war, under18_hold; random sample
speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
english: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, prepare yourself for battle. Then you will incur no sin.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
iast:
nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||
english: On this path no effort is wasted and no harm comes from falling short. Even a little of this practice protects a person from great fear.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ |
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ ||
english: The unwise, son of Pritha, who delight in the letter of the Vedas and claim there is nothing more, speak flowery words
codex_problem: “The letter of the Vedas” suggests literalism or a letter-versus-spirit contrast that is not stated by vedavādaratāḥ.
codex_sanskrit_says: The unwise delight in Vedic words or doctrine, speak this flowery speech, and maintain that nothing else exists.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām |
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||
english: Those who cling to pleasure and power, their minds carried away by such words, do not develop the resolute understanding that rests in deep concentration.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनंजय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanaṃjaya |
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ ||
english: Action done for its results is far inferior to the discipline of understanding, Arjuna. Seek refuge in that understanding; those whose motive is the result are pitiable.
codex_problem: The qualifier “done for its results” is not attached to “action” in the Sanskrit and narrows the first statement interpretively.
codex_sanskrit_says: Action is far inferior to the discipline of understanding; seek refuge in understanding, for those who make the fruit their motive are pitiable.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
iast:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim ||
english: Krishna, how would you describe a person of steady wisdom, settled in deep concentration? How does someone of steady mind speak, how do they sit, how do they move?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
iast:
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān |
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate ||
english: Son of Pritha, when a person gives up every desire that enters the mind and is content in the self, by the self, that person is said to be of steady wisdom.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||
english: What is night for all beings is the time of waking for the self-controlled; and when other beings are awake, that is night for the sage who truly sees.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati ||
english: This is the state of Brahman, son of Pritha. Having reached it, a person is never deluded again; remaining in it even at the hour of death, they attain the peace of Brahman.
codex_problem: “The peace of Brahman” softens and alters brahmanirvāṇa, which denotes final extinction or liberation in Brahman rather than merely peace.
codex_sanskrit_says: Remaining in this state even at the time of death, a person attains nirvana in Brahman.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
iast:
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana |
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava ||
english: Krishna, if you think that understanding is better than action, then why do you urge me into this terrible action?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate ||
english: One who holds back the organs of action but sits dwelling in the mind on the objects of the senses is deluded, and is called a hypocrite.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥
iast:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara ||
english: This world is bound by action, except for action done as sacrifice. So, son of Kunti, act for that purpose, free of attachment.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
iast:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||
english: Know that action arises from Brahman, and Brahman arises from the Imperishable. So the all-pervading Brahman is always established in sacrifice.
codex_problem: Here brahma refers to the Veda or sacred revelation, not to Brahman as the ultimate reality. Rendering it as “Brahman” makes Brahman arise from a separate Imperishable and obscures the verse’s sequence.
codex_sanskrit_says: Know that action arises from the Veda, and the Veda arises from the Imperishable; therefore the all-pervading Veda is always established in sacrifice.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
iast:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ||
english: Whoever does not keep turning the wheel set in motion in this way, son of Pritha, lives in vain, a sinful life of pleasing the senses.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
iast:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ ||
english: Such a person has nothing to gain in this world by acting and nothing to lose by not acting, and depends on no being for anything.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
iast:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā |
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ ||
english: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind on the self, free of desire and of any sense of 'mine', fight, with your fever of distress gone.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
iast:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ ||
english: But those who find fault with my teaching and do not follow it, know them to be confused about all knowledge, lost and without understanding.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
english: Better your own duty done imperfectly than another's duty done well. Better to die in your own duty; another's duty is full of danger.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
iast:
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ |
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam ||
english: It is desire; it is anger, born of the guna of rajas. All-devouring and deeply harmful, know it to be the enemy here.
codex_problem: “Deeply harmful” softens mahāpāpmā, which describes desire as greatly evil or a great source of sin, not merely harmful.
codex_sanskrit_says: This is desire, this is anger, born from the guna of rajas; it is all-devouring and greatly evil. Know it here as the enemy.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥
iast:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
english: To protect the good, to destroy those who do evil, and to establish dharma firmly, I come into being age after age.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
iast:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna ||
english: One who truly knows my divine birth and actions in this way is not born again on leaving the body, Arjuna, but comes to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
iast:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||
english: However people approach me, so I receive them. Everywhere, son of Pritha, people follow my path.
codex_problem: “Everywhere” makes sarvaśaḥ spatial, whereas it means “in every way.” Also, bhajāmi here means that Krishna responds to or reciprocates with people in the same manner as they approach him, not merely that he receives them.
codex_sanskrit_says: As people approach me, so in that very manner I respond to them; people follow my path in every way, O son of Pritha.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
iast:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā ||
english: Wanting success from their actions, people here worship the gods, because in the human world success born of action comes quickly.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
iast:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam ||
english: The four varnas were created by me according to the division of qualities and actions. Though I am their maker, know me as the non-doer, the unchanging.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
iast:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ |
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt ||
english: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. I will explain action to you; knowing it, you will be freed from harm.
codex_problem: “Harm” softens and changes aśubha, which here denotes evil or what is inauspicious, rather than harm in general.
codex_sanskrit_says: I will explain action to you; knowing it, you will be freed from evil.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
iast:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
english: Without expectations, with mind and body controlled, having given up all possessions, doing only what the body requires, one incurs no fault.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
iast:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā ||
english: The act of offering is Brahman, the offering is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire that is Brahman. Brahman is reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
codex_problem: The final phrase replaces samādhi—absorption or concentration in action as Brahman—with the looser and expanded idea of seeing Brahman “in every action.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Brahman alone is to be reached by one whose absorption is in action as Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
iast:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||
english: So many kinds of sacrifice are spread out before Brahman. Know them all to be born of action; knowing this, you will be set free.
codex_problem: “Before Brahman” mistranslates brahmaṇo mukhe, literally “in the mouth of Brahman,” commonly understood here as “in the Veda.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Thus sacrifices of many kinds are spread out in the mouth of Brahman; know them all to be born of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati ||
english: One who has faith, who is devoted to it and has mastered the senses, gains knowledge; having gained knowledge, one soon reaches supreme peace.
codex_problem: The pronoun “it” makes the person devoted to faith, whereas tatparaḥ refers to being intent on or devoted to the knowledge or goal in question.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who has faith, is intent on that knowledge or goal, and has controlled the senses gains knowledge and soon attains supreme peace.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
iast:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ ||
english: But the ignorant, the faithless and the doubting perish; for one who doubts, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
iast:
tasmādajñānasambhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ |
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata ||
english: So, with the sword of knowledge, cut away this doubt about the self, born of ignorance and lodged in your heart; take up yoga, and stand up, Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
iast:
yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate ||
english: The disciplined, giving up the fruit of action, attain lasting peace; the undisciplined, driven by desire and attached to the fruit, are bound.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
iast:
vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ ||
english: The wise see the same in a brahmin rich in learning and humility, in a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste who eats dogs.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसंकल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥
iast:
yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
na hyasaṃnyastasaṃkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||
english: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, son of Pandu; for no one becomes a yogi without renouncing selfish intentions.
codex_problem: “Selfish” is an added qualification: saṅkalpa means resolves, intentions, conceptions, or desires, without itself specifying selfishness.
codex_sanskrit_says: No one becomes a yogi without renouncing resolves or desires.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते ।
सर्वसंकल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥
iast:
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate |
sarvasaṃkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate ||
english: When a person is not attached to the objects of the senses or to actions, and has renounced all selfish intentions, they are said to have risen to yoga.
codex_problem: “Selfish” improperly narrows sarvasaṅkalpa: the verse says that all resolves, intentions, or desires have been renounced, not merely selfish ones.
codex_sanskrit_says: When one is attached neither to sense objects nor to actions and has renounced all resolves or desires, one is said to have risen to yoga.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
iast:
uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet |
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
english: Lift yourself up by your own effort, and do not let yourself sink. You alone are your own friend, and you alone are your own enemy.
codex_problem: “By your own effort” replaces the verse’s repeated and significant ātman language with an interpretation; effort is not stated in the Sanskrit.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should raise the self by the self and should not degrade the self, for the self alone is the self’s friend and the self alone is the self’s enemy.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
iast:
bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ |
anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
english: For one who has conquered themselves, the self is a friend; but for one who has not, the self acts with hostility, like an enemy.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ।
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
iast:
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ |
yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ ||
english: The yogi who is satisfied with knowledge and wisdom, unshakable, with senses mastered, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is called disciplined.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥
iast:
yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ ||
english: The yogi should constantly practise concentration, staying in a secluded place, alone, with mind and body controlled, without expectations and without possessions.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
iast:
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu |
yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā ||
english: For one who is moderate in eating and recreation, measured in effort at work, and moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
iast:
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ ||
english: "A lamp in a windless place does not flicker": that is the comparison used for the yogi of controlled mind, practising the yoga of the self.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
संकल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः ।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥
iast:
saṃkalpaprabhavānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ |
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ ||
english: Giving up completely all desires born of selfish intention, and restraining the whole range of the senses on every side by the mind alone,
codex_problem: “Selfish” is an interpretive addition: saṃkalpa does not itself mean selfish intention.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should completely abandon all desires born of mental conception, intention, or resolve, and restrain the entire group of senses on every side by the mind alone.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः ।
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥
iast:
yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ |
sukhena brahmasaṃsparśamatyantaṃ sukhamaśnute ||
english: Always practising in this way, the yogi, freed from impurity, easily attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति ।
अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
iast:
kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati |
apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi ||
english: Fallen from both, does such a person not perish like a scattered cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, lost on the path to Brahman?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः ।
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
iast:
etanme saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ |
tvadanyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate ||
english: Krishna, please dispel this doubt of mine completely; no one but you can dispel it.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
iast:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ |
māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ ||
english: Evildoers, the deluded, the lowest of people, whose knowledge is stolen by māyā and who have taken on a demonic nature, do not take refuge in me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये ।
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
iast:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye |
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam ||
english: Those who take refuge in me and strive for freedom from old age and death know Brahman fully, the inner self, and all of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः ।
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
iast:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ ||
english: Those who know me in relation to beings, to the gods and to sacrifice, their minds disciplined, know me even at the hour of death.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन ।
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥
iast:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana |
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ ||
english: Who is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, and how, Krishna? And how are you to be known at the hour of death by those who are self-controlled?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् ।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
iast:
antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram |
yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ ||
english: Whoever leaves the body at the time of death remembering me alone comes to my state of being; there is no doubt about this.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
iast:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram |
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ ||
english: Whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, son of Kunti, to that state they go, having always been absorbed in it.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
iast:
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca |
mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṃśayam ||
english: So at all times remember me, and fight. With your mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रयाणकाले मनसाचलेन ।
भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव ।
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् ।
स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
iast:
prayāṇakāle manasācalena |
bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva |
bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak |
sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam ||
english: at the time of death, with an unmoving mind, joined with devotion and the strength of yoga, setting the life-breath fully between the eyebrows, reaches that supreme divine Person.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
iast:
sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām ||
english: Closing all the gates of the body, holding the mind in the heart, drawing the life-breath into the head, established in yogic concentration,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् ।
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
iast:
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran |
yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
english: uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs, leaving the body, reaches the highest goal.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
iast:
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate |
rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame ||
english: This same multitude of beings, coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of night, son of Pritha, and arises again at the coming of day.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
iast:
avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim |
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama ||
english: This unmanifest is called the Imperishable; it is called the highest goal. Those who reach it do not return: that is my supreme abode.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः ।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ |
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha ||
english: Now I will tell you, best of the Bharatas, of the times at which yogis who depart either do not return or do return.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
iast:
agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam |
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ ||
english: Fire, light, day, the bright half of the month, the six months of the sun's northern course: departing by these, people who know Brahman go to Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
iast:
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam |
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate ||
english: Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months of the sun's southern course: by these the yogi reaches the light of the moon and returns.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः ॥
iast:
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate |
ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayāvartate punaḥ ||
english: These two paths, the bright and the dark, are held to be the world's eternal ways: by one a person goes and does not return; by the other a person comes back again.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥
iast:
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa |
aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani ||
english: People who have no faith in this dharma, scorcher of enemies, do not reach me but return to the path of death and worldly existence.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥
iast:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ |
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ ||
english: Their hopes in vain, their actions in vain, their knowledge in vain, senseless, they take on the deluding nature of rakshasas and asuras.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च ।
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥
iast:
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca |
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna ||
english: I give heat; I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and also death, being and non-being, Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ।
कौन्तेय प्रति जानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
iast:
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati |
kaunteya prati jānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati ||
english: They quickly become righteous and attain lasting peace. Know this for certain, son of Kunti: my devotee never perishes.
codex_problem: The imperative pratijānīhi tells Arjuna to declare or affirm this, not merely to know it for certain.
codex_sanskrit_says: O son of Kunti, declare: “My devotee never perishes.”

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
iast:
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ |
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim ||
english: For those who take refuge in me, son of Pritha, even those of sinful birth, women, vaishyas and shudras, they too reach the highest goal.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा ।
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥
iast:
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā |
anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām ||
english: How much more, then, holy brahmins and devoted royal sages! Having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
iast:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |
puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum ||
english: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier; the eternal divine Person, the first of the gods, unborn and all-pervading.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
iast:
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ ||
english: Among household priests, know me to be the chief, Brihaspati, son of Pritha; among generals I am Skanda; among bodies of water, the ocean.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥
iast:
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ ||
english: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows, the wish-granting cow; of procreators I am Kandarpa, the god of love; among serpents I am Vasuki.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥
iast:
pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham |
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī ||
english: Among purifiers I am the wind; among those who bear weapons, Rama; among sea creatures, the makara; and among rivers, the Ganga.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
iast:
mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ||
