vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ ||
english: Whether it is leaving the body, staying in it, or experiencing the world through the gunas, the deluded do not see it; those with the eye of knowledge see it.
codex_problem: The English changes “endowed or associated with the gunas” into “experiencing the world through the gunas,” adding “the world” and making the gunas the means of experience.
codex_sanskrit_says: The deluded do not perceive it as it departs, remains, or experiences while associated with the gunas; those with the eye of knowledge perceive it.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।
अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥
iast:
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram |
aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam ||
english: They say the world is without truth, without foundation, without a Lord, not brought about by any order: what else is it but driven by desire?
codex_problem: “Not brought about by any order” mistranslates aparasparasaṃbhūtam and omits its reference to mutual generation or union.
codex_sanskrit_says: They say that the world is unreal, without foundation and without a Lord, born of mutual union; what else could it be but caused by desire?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥
iast:
cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ |
kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ ||
english: Given over to boundless anxieties that end only with death, taking the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all there is,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
iast:
asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi |
īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī ||
english: That enemy has been killed by me, and I will kill others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer; I am successful, powerful and happy.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
iast:
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau ||
english: Bewildered by many thoughts, caught in the net of delusion, attached to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
iast:
ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam ||
english: Self-important, stubborn, full of pride and the intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, out of hypocrisy, not according to the rules.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रुरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
iast:
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krurānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu ||
english: These hateful, cruel, vilest of people, I hurl again and again into the cycles of rebirth, into demonic wombs alone.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
iast:
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim ||
english: Falling into demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, never reaching me, son of Kunti, they sink to the lowest state.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
दम्भाहंकारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥
iast:
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
dambhāhaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ ||
english: Those people who practise terrible austerities not prescribed by scripture, full of hypocrisy and ego, driven by the force of desire and passion,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥
iast:
karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ |
māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān ||
english: senselessly tormenting the elements in the body, and me too, who dwell within the body: know them to be of demonic resolve.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
iast:
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam |
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate ||
english: Reverence for the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, honesty, celibacy and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||
english: Austerity practised out of foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to bring ruin on another, is called tamasic.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥
iast:
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana ||
english: Mighty-armed one, I wish to know the truth about renunciation, Krishna, and about relinquishment, and how they differ.
codex_problem: “How they differ” is an interpretive addition: pṛthak asks to know the two separately. The rendering also replaces the distinct epithets Hṛṣīkeśa and Keśiniṣūdana with “Krishna,” losing their stated senses.
codex_sanskrit_says: Arjuna asks the mighty-armed Hṛṣīkeśa, slayer of Keśin, to explain separately the true nature of renunciation and of relinquishment.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
iast:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit ||
english: Unwanted, wanted and mixed: the fruit of action is of three kinds, and it comes after death to those who have not relinquished, but never to those who have renounced.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
iast:
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvāpi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate ||
english: One who is free of the sense of 'I am the doer', whose understanding is not tainted, even if they kill these people, does not kill and is not bound.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
iast:
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ |
viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate ||
english: A doer who is undisciplined, coarse, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is called tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनंजय ॥
iast:
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya ||
english: Now hear, Arjuna, the threefold division of understanding and of fortitude according to the gunas, explained fully and separately.
codex_problem: “Arjuna” identifies the addressee but omits the meaning of the epithet Dhanañjaya.
codex_sanskrit_says: Krishna addresses him as Dhanañjaya, “conqueror of wealth.”

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
iast:
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī ||
english: The fortitude by which a foolish person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and arrogance, son of Pritha, is tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
iast:
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati ||
english: Now hear from me, best of the Bharatas, about the three kinds of happiness: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, in which sorrow comes to an end,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप ।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ ||
english: The duties of brahmins, kshatriyas and vaishyas, and of shudras too, Arjuna, are divided according to the gunas that arise from their own nature.
codex_problem: “Arjuna” identifies the addressee but omits the meaning of the epithet Parantapa.
codex_sanskrit_says: Krishna addresses him as Parantapa, “scorcher of foes.”

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam ||
english: Calm, self-restraint, austerity, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, insight and faith are the work of a brahmin, born of their nature.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam ||
english: Courage, vigour, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity and leadership are the work of a kshatriya, born of their nature.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam ||
english: Farming, tending cattle and trade are the work of a vaishya, born of their nature; and work that consists of service is the shudra's, also born of their nature.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
iast:
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu ||
english: Each devoted to their own work, a person attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to their own work finds perfection.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
iast:
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ ||
english: By worshipping, through their own work, the one from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
english: Better one's own dharma, though imperfect, than another's dharma well performed. Doing the work set by one's own nature, one incurs no fault.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
iast:
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ ||
english: Do not give up the work you were born to, son of Kunti, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by fault, as fire is by smoke.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati ||
english: One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered themselves and is free of craving, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्ध्या युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
iast:
buddhyā viśuddhyā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca ||
english: Endowed with a purified understanding, controlling oneself with steadiness, turning away from sound and the other objects of the senses, and casting aside attraction and aversion,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
iast:
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ ||
english: living in solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body and mind controlled, always intent on the yoga of meditation, taking refuge in dispassion,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
english: letting go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, free of the sense of 'mine' and at peace, one becomes fit to attain the state of Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
iast:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava ||
english: Mentally offering all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहंकारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
iast:
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṃkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi ||
english: With your mind on me, you will cross every difficulty by my grace; but if out of ego you will not listen, you will be lost.
codex_problem: “You will be lost” softens the stronger warning expressed by vinaṅkṣyasi.
codex_sanskrit_says: If out of ego you do not listen, you will perish or be destroyed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
iast:
yadahaṃkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati ||
english: If, relying on ego, you think 'I will not fight', that resolve of yours is in vain: your own nature will compel you.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
iast:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat ||
english: Bound by your own action, born of your nature, son of Kunti, what you do not wish to do out of delusion you will do, even against your will.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
iast:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
english: Let go of all dharmas and take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥
iast:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ ||
english: And whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by them I would be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge: that is my view.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
iast:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta |
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava ||
english: My delusion is gone, Krishna; by your grace I have regained clear understanding. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.
codex_problem: Smṛti is rendered as “clear understanding,” replacing the verse’s explicit statement that memory or recollection has been regained.
codex_sanskrit_says: My delusion is destroyed, and by your grace I have regained memory, O Achyuta. I stand firm, free from doubt, and will do as you say.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
iast:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahān rājanhṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
english: And as I recall again and again that most wondrous form of Krishna, great is my amazement, O king, and I rejoice again and again.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
iast:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama ||
english: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is the son of Pritha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and lasting good policy: that is my conviction.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
असुर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसाऽऽवृताः ।
ताँस्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्ति ये के चात्महनो जनाः ॥
iast:
asuryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā''vṛtāḥ |
tām̐ste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ ||
english: Those worlds called demonic are covered in blind darkness. To them, after death, go all those people who slay the self.

speaker: seeker
devanagari:
वायुरनिलममृतमथेदं भस्मांतँ शरीरम् ।
ॐ क्रतो स्मर कृतँ स्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतँ स्मर ॥
iast:
vāyuranilamamṛtamathedaṃ bhasmāṃtam̐ śarīram |
oṃ krato smara kṛtam̐ smara krato smara kṛtam̐ smara ||
english: Now let my breath go to the immortal wind, and let this body end in ashes. Om. O mind, remember! Remember what was done! O mind, remember! Remember what was done!

speaker: teacher
devanagari:
श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद्वाचो ह वाचं
स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश्चक्षुः ।
अतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
iast:
śrotrasya śrotraṃ manaso mano yadvāco ha vācaṃ
sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaścakṣuḥ |
atimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ||
english: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech; it is the breath of breath and the eye of the eye. Letting go, the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.

speaker: teacher
devanagari:
यच्छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रमिदं श्रुतम् ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast:
yacchrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutam |
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ||
english: What one cannot hear with the ear, but by which this ear is heard: know that alone as Brahman, not this which people worship here.

speaker: teacher
devanagari:
यदि मन्यसे सुवेदेति दहरमेवापि
नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपम् ।
यदस्य त्वं यदस्य देवेष्वथ नु
मीमाँस्येमेव ते मन्ये विदितम् ॥
iast:
yadi manyase suvedeti daharamevāpi
nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam |
yadasya tvaṃ yadasya deveṣvatha nu
mīmām̐syemeva te manye viditam ||
english: If you think, 'I know it well,' then surely you know only a little of Brahman's form: the form that is in you, and the form that is among the gods. So I think you must still inquire into it. 'I think I know it.'
codex_problem: The English uses मन्ये (“I think”) twice—once in the teacher’s injunction and again in the closing reply—although it occurs only once in the Sanskrit.
codex_sanskrit_says: On the dialogue reading, the teacher says that it must still be investigated by the student, after which the student replies, “I think it is known.”

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
इह चेदवेदीदथ सत्यमस्ति
न चेदिहावेदीन्महती विनष्टिः ।
भूतेषु भूतेषु विचित्य धीराः
प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
iast:
iha cedavedīdatha satyamasti
na cedihāvedīnmahatī vinaṣṭiḥ |
bhūteṣu bhūteṣu vicitya dhīrāḥ
pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ||
english: If one knows it here, then there is truth; if one does not know it here, great is the loss. Discerning it in every being, the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.

speaker: narrator
devanagari:
ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो
विजये देवा अमहीयन्त ॥
iast:
brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo
vijaye devā amahīyanta ||
english: Brahman, it is told, won a victory for the gods, and in Brahman's victory the gods grew great.

speaker: narrator
devanagari:
तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतदादत्स्वेति
तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाकादतुम् ।
स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
iast:
tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetadādatsveti
tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśākādatum |
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ||
english: It set a blade of grass before him: 'Carry this off.' He went at it with all his speed but could not move it. He turned back from there: 'I could not find out what this wondrous being is.'
codex_problem: “Could not move it” strengthens and changes the Sanskrit, which does not say that the grass could not be moved at all.
codex_sanskrit_says: Vayu approached with all his speed but could not take up or carry away the blade of grass.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
तस्यैष आदेशो यदेतद्विद्युतो व्यद्युतदा३इतीन् न्यमीमिषदा३
इत्यधिदैवतम् ॥
iast:
tasyaiṣa ādeśo yadetadvidyuto vyadyutadā3itīn nyamīmiṣadā3
ityadhidaivatam ||
english: This is the teaching about it, by likeness: as it flashed in the lightning, ah! as it made the eye blink, ah! This is with regard to the divine.

speaker: narrator
devanagari:
ॐ उशन् ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ ।
तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस ॥
iast:
oṃ uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau |
tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa ||
english: Om. Wanting its reward, the son of Vajashravas, it is told, gave away all he owned. He had a son named Nachiketas.
codex_problem: “Wanting its reward” supplies a specific object for उशन् (“desiring”) that the Sanskrit does not state; no rite or its reward is explicitly mentioned here.
codex_sanskrit_says: Vajashravas’s descendant, desiring, gave away all his possessions; he had a son named Nachiketas.

speaker: narrator
devanagari:
स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति ।
द्वितीयं तृतीयं तँ होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति ॥
iast:
sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti |
dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tam̐ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti ||
english: He said to his father, 'Father, to whom will you give me?' He said it a second time, and a third. His father said to him, 'To Death I give you!'

speaker: Nachiketas
devanagari:
बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः ।
किँ स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाऽद्य करिष्यति ॥
iast:
bahūnāmemi prathamo bahūnāmemi madhyamaḥ |
kim̐ svidyamasya kartavyaṃ yanmayā'dya kariṣyati ||
english: Among many I go as the first; among many I go as one of the middle. What work does Yama have that he will do through me today?

speaker: Nachiketas
devanagari:
अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथाऽपरे ।
सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः ॥
iast:
anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathā'pare |
sasyamiva martyaḥ pacyate sasyamivājāyate punaḥ ||
english: Look back at how those before us acted; look around at how others act now. A mortal ripens like grain, and like grain is born again.

speaker: Yama's household
devanagari:
वैश्वानरः प्रविशत्यतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान् ।
तस्यैताँ शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम् ॥
iast:
vaiśvānaraḥ praviśatyatithirbrāhmaṇo gṛhān |
tasyaitām̐ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam ||
english: A brahmin guest enters houses like fire itself. People make this offering of peace to him: bring water, son of Vivasvat!

speaker: Yama's household
devanagari:
आशाप्रतीक्षे संगतँ सूनृतां
चेष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूँश्च सर्वान् ।
एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो
यस्यानश्नन्वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे ॥
iast:
āśāpratīkṣe saṃgatam̐ sūnṛtāṃ
ceṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūm̐śca sarvān |
etadvṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso
yasyānaśnanvasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe ||
english: Hopes and expectations, the fruit of good company, kind speech, sacrifices and good works, sons and cattle: all these are taken from the person of little understanding in whose house a brahmin stays without food.

speaker: Nachiketas
devanagari:
शान्तसंकल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्
वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माऽभि मृत्यो ।
त्वत्प्रसृष्टम् माऽभिवदेत्प्रतीत
एतत् त्रयाणां प्रथमं वरं वृणे ॥
iast:
śāntasaṃkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād
vītamanyurgautamo mā'bhi mṛtyo |
tvatprasṛṣṭam mā'bhivadetpratīta
etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe ||
english: That Gautama, my father, may be calm in mind, cheerful, and free of anger towards me, O Death; that he may recognise and greet me when you send me back: this I choose as the first of the three boons.
codex_problem: “My father” is supplied by the English; this verse names Gautama but does not explicitly identify him as the speaker’s father.
codex_sanskrit_says: May Gautama be calm in mind, cheerful, and free of anger toward me; when sent back by you, may I be recognised and greeted by him.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा
य एवं विद्वाँश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् ।
स मृत्युपाशान् पुरतः प्रणोद्य
शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ॥
iast:
triṇāciketastrayametadviditvā
ya evaṃ vidvām̐ścinute nāciketam |
sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya
śokātigo modate svargaloke ||
english: One who knows these three and, knowing this, builds the Nachiketa fire, casts off the nooses of death beforehand and, beyond sorrow, rejoices in the heaven-world.
codex_problem: The English misrepresents or omits triṇāciketaḥ, which denotes one who has performed or kindled the Nachiketa fire three times, not simply one who “knows these three.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The threefold Nachiketa practitioner, having known this triad and knowingly building the Nachiketa fire, casts off the nooses of death and rejoices beyond sorrow in heaven.

speaker: Nachiketas
devanagari:
येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये-
ऽस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके ।
एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाऽहं
वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः ॥
iast:
yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye-
'stītyeke nāyamastīti caike |
etadvidyāmanuśiṣṭastvayā'haṃ
varāṇāmeṣa varastṛtīyaḥ ||
english: There is this doubt about a person who has died: some say 'he is', others say 'he is not'. Taught by you, I would know this. This is the third of my boons.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके
सर्वान् कामाँश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व ।
इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या
न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः ।
आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व
नचिकेतो मरणं माऽनुप्राक्षीः ॥
iast:
ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke
sarvān kāmām̐śchandataḥ prārthayasva |
imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā
na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ |
ābhirmatprattābhiḥ paricārayasva
naciketo maraṇaṃ mā'nuprākṣīḥ ||
english: Whatever desires are hard to win in the world of mortals, ask for them all as you wish: these lovely women with chariots and music, such as no mortal can obtain. Be served by them, my gift to you. Nachiketas, do not ask about death.

speaker: Nachiketas
devanagari:
यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो
यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् ।
योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो
नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते ॥
iast:
yasminnidaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo
yatsāmparāye mahati brūhi nastat |
yo'yaṃ varo gūḍhamanupraviṣṭo
nānyaṃ tasmānnaciketā vṛṇīte ||
english: That about which people doubt, Death, concerning the great passing beyond: tell us that. This boon, which enters into what is hidden: Nachiketas chooses no other.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं
प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् ।
अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी
पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे ॥
iast:
na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ
pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham |
ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī
punaḥ punarvaśamāpadyate me ||
english: The passage beyond does not shine for the childish, careless and deluded by wealth. 'This world exists, there is no other,' thinks such a person, and falls into my power again and again.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
कामस्याप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां
क्रतोरानन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् ।
स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा
धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ॥
iast:
kāmasyāptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ
kratorānantyamabhayasya pāram |
stomamahadurugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā
dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo'tyasrākṣīḥ ||
english: You saw the fulfilment of desire, the foundation of the world, the endless fruit of ritual, the far shore of fearlessness, the great and praised wide path, the firm standing; and, wise and steadfast, Nachiketas, you let them all go.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः
प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य ।
स मोदते मोदनीयँ हि लब्ध्वा
विवृतँ सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये ॥
iast:
etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ
pravṛhya dharmyamaṇumetamāpya |
sa modate modanīyam̐ hi labdhvā
vivṛtam̐ sadma naciketasaṃ manye ||
english: A mortal who has heard this, grasped it fully, drawn out this subtle Self that is true to dharma, and reached it, rejoices, having found what is truly worth rejoicing in. I think the house stands open for Nachiketas.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्
नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin
nāyaṃ kutaścinna babhūva kaścit |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
english: The wise one is not born and does not die. It did not come from anywhere, and nothing came from it. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुँ हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायँ हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
iast:
hantā cenmanyate hantum̐ hataścenmanyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyam̐ hanti na hanyate ||
english: If the killer thinks he kills, and if the one killed thinks he is killed, neither of them understands: this does not kill, and is not killed.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः ।
नाशान्तमानसो वाऽपि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥
iast:
nāvirato duścaritānnāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ |
nāśāntamānaso vā'pi prajñānenainamāpnuyāt ||
english: One who has not turned away from wrongdoing, who is not calm, not collected, whose mind is not at peace, cannot reach it through knowledge.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः ।
मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः ॥
iast:
yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ |
mṛtyuryasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ ||
english: For whom priesthood and kingship are both just rice, and death is the sauce poured on it: who, like this, knows where it is?

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके
गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे ।
छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति
पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः ॥
iast:
ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke
guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe |
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti
pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ ||
english: Two drink the truth of their deeds in the world of good works, having entered the secret place, the highest seat. Knowers of Brahman call them shadow and light, as do householders who keep the five fires and those who have thrice kindled the Nachiketa fire.
codex_problem: Here ṛtam is the recompense or fruit of deeds, not “the truth of their deeds.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The two drink the recompense of deeds in the world of good works, having entered the secret place in the highest realm.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः ।
न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
yastvavijñānavānbhavatyamanaskaḥ sadā'śuciḥ |
na sa tatpadamāpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati ||
english: Whoever lacks understanding, is unmindful and always impure, does not reach that goal, but goes on into the round of rebirth.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद् ब्रह्मसंसदि ।
प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते ।
तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति ॥
iast:
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi |
prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tadānantyāya kalpate |
tadānantyāya kalpata iti ||
english: Whoever, purified, recites this supreme secret in an assembly of brahmins or at the time of the rites for the dead, gains what is endless; gains what is endless.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बाला-
स्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् ।
अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा
ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥
iast:
parācaḥ kāmānanuyanti bālā-
ste mṛtyoryanti vitatasya pāśam |
atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā
dhruvamadhruveṣviha na prārthayante ||
english: The childish run after outward pleasures and walk into the wide-spread net of death. But the wise, knowing what is truly immortal, seek nothing here among the unstable things.
codex_problem: “Seek nothing” is broader than the Sanskrit and omits the object dhruvam, “the permanent.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The wise, having recognized immortality, do not seek the permanent here among impermanent things.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शाँश्च मैथुनान् ।
एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśām̐śca maithunān |
etenaiva vijānāti kimatra pariśiṣyate |
etadvai tat ||
english: That by which one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touches and the pleasures of love: by this alone one knows. What remains here? This, truly, is that.
codex_problem: “The pleasures of love” softens and changes maithunān, which refers specifically to sexual unions or intercourse.
codex_sanskrit_says: By that one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touches, and sexual unions.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥
iast:
yadeveha tadamutra yadamutra tadanviha |
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
english: What is here is there; what is there is here. Whoever sees difference here goes from death to death.
codex_problem: The translation omits iva, “as if,” and therefore loses the verse’s indication that the perceived plurality is only apparent.
codex_sanskrit_says: Whoever sees here as if there were plurality goes from death to death.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानाऽस्ति किंचन ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥
iast:
manasaivedamāptavyaṃ neha nānā'sti kiṃcana |
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
english: By the mind alone is this to be reached: there is no difference here at all. Whoever sees difference here goes from death to death.
codex_problem: The translation omits iva, “as if,” and therefore loses the verse’s indication that the perceived plurality is only apparent.
codex_sanskrit_says: There is no plurality here at all; whoever sees here as if there were plurality goes from death to death.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः ।
देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ |
dehādvimucyamānasya kimatra pariśiṣyate |
etadvai tat ||
english: When this embodied one, dwelling in the body, slips away and is freed from the body, what remains here? This, truly, is that.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥
iast:
hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam |
yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ||
english: Now, Gautama, I will tell you this secret, eternal Brahman, and what becomes of the self after reaching death.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः ।
स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ॥
iast:
yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ |
sthāṇumanye'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ||
english: Some embodied beings enter a womb to take on a body; others pass into a stationary thing, according to their deeds and according to their knowledge.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
ūrdhvamūlo'vākśākha eṣo'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ |
tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate |
tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana |
etadvai tat ||
english: This is the ancient fig tree, with roots above and branches below. That is the bright, that is Brahman, that alone is called immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it. This, truly, is that.
codex_problem: “Ancient” weakens sanātana, which means eternal or everlasting, not merely very old.
codex_sanskrit_says: This is the eternal aśvattha tree, with its root above and branches below.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः ।
भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ॥
iast:
bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ |
bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ||
english: From fear of it fire burns; from fear the sun gives heat; from fear Indra and the Wind, and Death as the fifth, run their course.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्षरीरस्य विस्रसः ।
ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
iha cedaśakadboddhuṃ prākṣarīrasya visrasaḥ |
tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ||
english: If one can come to know it here, before the body falls away, [one is freed]; otherwise one becomes fit to take a body again in the created worlds.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥
iast:
indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvamuttamam |
sattvādadhi mahānātmā mahato'vyaktamuttamam ||
english: Beyond the senses is the mind; beyond the mind is the intellect, the highest; beyond the intellect is the great self; beyond the great is the unmanifest, the highest.
codex_problem: Calling both the intellect and the unmanifest “the highest” gives them absolute supremacy and conflicts with the hierarchy stated in this and the following verse. Here uttamam has a relational sense: each is higher than the preceding principle.
codex_sanskrit_says: The mind is beyond the senses; the intellect is higher than the mind; the great Self is above the intellect; and the unmanifest is higher than the great Self.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्य-
स्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका ।
तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति
विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति ॥
iast:
śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍya-
stāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā |
tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti
viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti ||
english: A hundred and one are the channels of the heart; one of them goes up to the crown of the head. Going up by it, one reaches immortality; the others lead in every direction at the time of departure.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः ।
ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्माऽपि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
iast:
ajñaḥ sukhamārādhyaḥ sukhataramārādhyate viśeṣajñaḥ |
jñānalavadurvidagdhaṃ brahmā'pi taṃ naraṃ na rañjayati ||
english: An ignorant person is easily persuaded; an expert is persuaded more easily still; but someone puffed up by a scrap of knowledge, not even Brahma himself can win over.
codex_problem: ārādhya and rañjayati concern pleasing, satisfying, or winning someone over, not persuading them intellectually.
codex_sanskrit_says: An ignorant person is easily pleased, and an expert still more easily; but not even Brahma can please or win over a person made conceited by a little knowledge.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कृमिकुलचितं लालाक्लिन्नं विगन्धि जुगुप्सितं निरुपमरसं प्रीत्या खादन्नरास्थि निरामिषम्।
सुरपतिमपि श्वा पार्श्वस्थं विलोक्य न शङ्कते न हि गणयति क्षुद्रो जन्तुः परिग्रहफल्गुताम् ॥
iast:
kṛmikulacitaṃ lālāklinnaṃ vigandhi jugupsitaṃ nirupamarasaṃ prītyā khādannarāsthi nirāmiṣam|
surapatimapi śvā pārśvasthaṃ vilokya na śaṅkate na hi gaṇayati kṣudro jantuḥ parigrahaphalgutām ||
english: Gnawing with relish a human bone, crawling with worms, wet with saliva, foul-smelling, disgusting and without meat, a dog does not flinch even at Indra standing beside it; a petty creature does not see how worthless its possession is.
codex_problem: The rendering omits nirupamarasam, which describes the bone as having incomparable flavour, in addition to saying that the dog eats it with relish.
codex_sanskrit_says: The dog gladly eats a meatless human bone that is worm-covered, saliva-soaked, foul-smelling and disgusting, yet of incomparable flavour; it does not heed even Indra nearby, since a petty creature does not recognize the worthlessness of its possession.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
साहित्यसङ्गीतकलाविहीनः साक्षात्पशुः पुच्छविषाणहीनः।
तृणं न खादन्नपि जीवमान-स्तद्भागधेयं परमं पशूनाम् ॥
iast:
sāhityasaṅgītakalāvihīnaḥ sākṣātpaśuḥ pucchaviṣāṇahīnaḥ|
tṛṇaṃ na khādannapi jīvamāna-stadbhāgadheyaṃ paramaṃ paśūnām ||
english: One without literature, music or art is plainly an animal without tail or horns; that it lives without eating grass is the great good fortune of the animals.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
येषां न विद्या न तपो न दानं ज्ञानं न शीलं न गुणो न धर्मः।
ते मर्त्यलोके भुवि भारभूता मनुष्यरूपेण मृगाश्चरन्ति ॥
iast:
yeṣāṃ na vidyā na tapo na dānaṃ jñānaṃ na śīlaṃ na guṇo na dharmaḥ|
te martyaloke bhuvi bhārabhūtā manuṣyarūpeṇa mṛgāścaranti ||
english: Those who have no learning, no discipline, no generosity, no knowledge, no good character, no virtue and no dharma are a burden on the earth in the world of mortals; they roam about as beasts in human form.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
क्षान्तिश्चेद्वचनेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां
ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद्दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम्।
किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्याऽनवद्या यदि
व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥
iast:
kṣāntiścedvacanena kiṃ kimaribhiḥ krodho'sti ceddehināṃ
jñātiścedanalena kiṃ yadi suhṛddivyauṣadhaiḥ kiṃ phalam|
kiṃ sarpairyadi durjanāḥ kimu dhanairvidyā'navadyā yadi
vrīḍā cetkimu bhūṣaṇaiḥ sukavitā yadyasti rājyena kim ||
english: If one has forbearance, what need of armour? If anger, what need of enemies? If kin, what need of fire? If a true friend, what use are divine medicines? If wicked people are near, what need of snakes? If one has faultless learning, what use is wealth? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
codex_problem: The supplied Sanskrit has vacanena, “speech” or “words,” not kavacena, “armour”; the English silently follows a different reading.
codex_sanskrit_says: As the text stands, it asks: “If there is forbearance, what need is there of speech?” The remaining comparisons are rendered correctly.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
दाक्षिण्यं स्वजने दया परजने शाठ्यं सदा दुर्जने
प्रीतिः साधुजने नयो नृपजने विद्वज्जनेष्वार्जवम्।
शौर्यं शत्रुजने क्षमा गुरुजने कान्ताजने धृष्टता,
ये चैवं पुरुषाः कलासु कुशलास्तेष्वेव लोकस्थितिः ॥
iast:
dākṣiṇyaṃ svajane dayā parajane śāṭhyaṃ sadā durjane
prītiḥ sādhujane nayo nṛpajane vidvajjaneṣvārjavam|
śauryaṃ śatrujane kṣamā gurujane kāntājane dhṛṣṭatā,
ye caivaṃ puruṣāḥ kalāsu kuśalāsteṣveva lokasthitiḥ ||
english: Courtesy towards one's own people, kindness towards strangers, cunning always towards the wicked, affection for the good, tact with those in power, straightforwardness with the learned, courage against enemies, forbearance towards elders, boldness with women: the world rests on people skilled in these arts.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निक्लेशलेशं मनः।
आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपहारिणीष्टदहरौ संप्राप्यते देहिना ॥
iast:
sūnuḥ saccaritaḥ satī priyatamā svāmī prasādonmukhaḥ snigdhaṃ mitramavañcakaḥ parijano nikleśaleśaṃ manaḥ|
ākāro ruciraḥ sthiraśca vibhavo vidyāvadātaṃ mukhaṃ tuṣṭe viṣṭapahāriṇīṣṭadaharau saṃprāpyate dehinā ||
english: A son of good conduct, a faithful beloved, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, honest servants, a mind without the least distress, a pleasing appearance, steady wealth, a face made bright by learning: these come to an embodied being when Vishnu, who grants all wishes, is pleased.
codex_problem: The English omits the epithet viṣṭapahārin, “taker-away or destroyer of the world,” applied to Hari.
codex_sanskrit_says: All the listed blessings are obtained when wish-granting Hari, the taker-away of the world, is pleased.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम्।
विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
iast:
asanto nābhyarthyāḥ suhṛdapi na yācyaḥ kṛśadhanaḥ priyā nyāyyā vṛttirmalinamasubhaṅge'pyasukaram|
vipadyuccaiḥ stheyaṃ padamanuvidheyaṃ ca mahatāṃ satāṃ kenoddiṣṭaṃ viṣamamasidhārāvratamidam ||
english: The wicked are not to be begged from; a friend with little money is not to be asked; one's living should be just and dear to one; a wrong act should be avoided even at the cost of life; in adversity, stand tall; follow the path of the great. Who taught the good this hard vow, like walking on a sword's edge?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
परिवर्तिनि संसारे मृतः को वा न जायते।
स जातो येन जातेन याति वंशः समुन्नतिम् ॥
iast:
parivartini saṃsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate|
sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṃśaḥ samunnatim ||
english: In this turning world, who that has died is not born again? That one alone is born by whose birth the family rises to greatness.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
वरं पक्षच्छेदः समदमघवन्मुक्तकुलिश-प्रहारैरुद्गच्छद्बहुलदहनोद्गारगुरुभिः।
तुषाराद्रेः सूनोरहह ! पितरि क्लेशविवशे न चासौ सम्पातः पयसि पयसां पत्युरुचितः ॥
iast:
varaṃ pakṣacchedaḥ samadamaghavanmuktakuliśa-prahārairudgacchadbahuladahanodgāragurubhiḥ|
tuṣārādreḥ sūnorahaha ! pitari kleśavivaśe na cāsau sampātaḥ payasi payasāṃ patyurucitaḥ ||
english: Better to have one's wings cut off by blows of the proud Indra's thunderbolt, heavy with bursting flames, than this: that the son of the snowy mountain, while his father suffered helplessly, should drop into the waters of the ocean. That was not fitting.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात्सुतो लालना- द्विप्रोऽनध्ययनात्कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात्।
ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्रया- न्मैत्री चाप्रणयात्समृद्धिरनयात्त्यागात्प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥
iast:
daurmantryānnṛpatirvinaśyati yatiḥ saṅgātsuto lālanā- dvipro'nadhyayanātkulaṃ kutanayācchīlaṃ khalopāsanāt|
hrīrmadyādanavekṣaṇādapi kṛṣiḥ snehaḥ pravāsāśrayā- nmaitrī cāpraṇayātsamṛddhiranayāttyāgātpramādāddhanam ||
english: A king is ruined by bad counsel, an ascetic by attachment, a son by pampering, a brahmin by not studying, a family by a bad son, good conduct by serving the wicked, modesty by drink, farming by neglect, affection by living away, friendship by lack of warmth, prosperity by misrule, and wealth by careless spending.
codex_problem: “Careless spending” merges two separate causes, tyāga and pramāda, and therefore omits their distinction.
codex_sanskrit_says: Wealth is ruined through relinquishing or giving it away and through negligence or carelessness.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
मणिः शाणोल्लीढः समरविजयी हेतिनिहतो मदक्षीणो नागः शरदि सरितः श्यानपुलिनाः।
कलाशेषश्चन्द्रः सुरतमृदिता बालललना स्तनिम्ना शोभन्ते गलितविभवाश्चार्थिषु जनाः ॥
iast:
maṇiḥ śāṇollīḍhaḥ samaravijayī hetinihato madakṣīṇo nāgaḥ śaradi saritaḥ śyānapulināḥ|
kalāśeṣaścandraḥ suratamṛditā bālalalanā stanimnā śobhante galitavibhavāścārthiṣu janāḥ ||
english: A gem polished on the whetstone, a victor wounded in battle, an elephant spent after rut, rivers with dry banks in autumn, the moon reduced to a sliver, a young woman tired from love-making, and people who have given away their wealth to those in need: these shine in their thinness.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात्सम्पूर्णो गणयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम्।
अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
iast:
parikṣīṇaḥ kaścitspṛhayati yavānāṃ prasṛtaye sa paścātsampūrṇo gaṇayati dharitrīṃ tṛṇasamām|
ataścānaikāntyādgurulaghutayā'rtheṣu dhaninā- mavasthā vastūni prathayati ca saṅkocayati ca ||
english: A destitute person longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, the same person counts the whole earth as worth a straw. So, because nothing is fixed, the circumstances of the wealthy make things seem great or small, expanding them and shrinking them.
codex_problem: “When full” misleadingly suggests physical satiety; sampūrṇa here contrasts with destitution and means having become prosperous or wealthy.
codex_sanskrit_says: A destitute person longs for a handful of barley, but after becoming prosperous regards the entire earth as no more valuable than grass.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
सत्यानृता च परुषा प्रियवादिनी च हिंस्रा दयालुरपि चार्थपरा वदान्या।
नित्यव्यया प्रचुरनित्यधनागमा च वाराङ्गनेव नृपनीतिरनेकरूपा ॥
iast:
satyānṛtā ca paruṣā priyavādinī ca hiṃsrā dayālurapi cārthaparā vadānyā|
nityavyayā pracuranityadhanāgamā ca vārāṅganeva nṛpanītiranekarūpā ||
english: Truthful and false, harsh and sweet-spoken, cruel and kind, grasping and generous, always spending yet always gathering wealth: the policy of kings has many forms, like a courtesan.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
आज्ञा कीर्तिः पालनं ब्राह्मणानां दानं भोगो मित्रसंरक्षणञ्च।
येषामेते षड्गुणा न प्रवृत्ताः कोऽर्थस्तेषां पार्थिवोपाश्रयेण ॥
iast:
ājñā kīrtiḥ pālanaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ dānaṃ bhogo mitrasaṃrakṣaṇañca|
yeṣāmete ṣaḍguṇā na pravṛttāḥ ko'rthasteṣāṃ pārthivopāśrayeṇa ||
english: Command, fame, protection of brahmins, generosity, enjoyment and protecting friends: for those in whom these six qualities are not active, what is the use of relying on a king?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत्प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम्।
तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृद्य्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥
iast:
yaddhātrā nijabhālapaṭṭalikhitaṃ stokaṃ mahadvā dhanaṃ tatprāpnoti marusthale'pi nitarāṃ merau tato nādhikam|
taddhīro bhava vittavatsu kṛpaṇāṃ vṛttiṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ kūpe paśya payonidhāvapi ghaṭo gṛdyṇāti tulyaṃ jalam ||
english: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on one's forehead, one gets it even in the desert, and on Mount Meru no more than that. So be steady; do not humble yourself in vain before the wealthy. See: whether in a well or in the ocean, a pot holds the same amount of water.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
लोभश्चेदगुणेन किं पिशुनता यद्यस्ति किं पातकैःसत्यं चेत्तपसा च किं शुचि मनो यद्यस्ति तीर्थेन किम्।
सौजन्यं यदि किं निजैः सुमहिमा यद्यस्ति किं मण्डनैः सद्विद्या यदि किं धनैरपयशो यद्यस्ति किं मृत्युना ॥
iast:
lobhaścedaguṇena kiṃ piśunatā yadyasti kiṃ pātakaiḥsatyaṃ cettapasā ca kiṃ śuci mano yadyasti tīrthena kim|
saujanyaṃ yadi kiṃ nijaiḥ sumahimā yadyasti kiṃ maṇḍanaiḥ sadvidyā yadi kiṃ dhanairapayaśo yadyasti kiṃ mṛtyunā ||
english: If there is greed, what need of other vices? If slander, what need of sins? If truth, what need of austerity? If the mind is pure, what need of pilgrimage? If goodness, what need of kin? If greatness, what need of ornaments? If true learning, what need of wealth? If disgrace, what need of death?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
शशी दिवसधूसरो गलितयौवना कामिनी सरो विगतवारिजं मुखमनक्षरं स्वाकृतेः।
प्रभुर्धनपरायणः सततदुर्गतः सज्जनो नृपाङ्गनगतः खलो मनसि सप्त शल्यानि मे ॥
iast:
śaśī divasadhūsaro galitayauvanā kāminī saro vigatavārijaṃ mukhamanakṣaraṃ svākṛteḥ|
prabhurdhanaparāyaṇaḥ satatadurgataḥ sajjano nṛpāṅganagataḥ khalo manasi sapta śalyāni me ||
english: The moon grey in daytime, a lovely woman whose youth has passed, a lake without lotuses, a handsome face without learning, a master bent only on money, a good person always in hardship, and a wicked person at the king's court: these seven are thorns in my mind.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
उद्भासिताऽखिलखलस्य विश्रृङ्खलस्य प्राग्जातविस्तृतनिजाधमकर्मवृत्तेः।
दैवादवाप्तविभवस्य गुणद्विषोऽस्य नीचस्य गोचरगतैः सुखमाप्यते कैः ॥
iast:
udbhāsitā'khilakhalasya viśrṛṅkhalasya prāgjātavistṛtanijādhamakarmavṛtteḥ|
daivādavāptavibhavasya guṇadviṣo'sya nīcasya gocaragataiḥ sukhamāpyate kaiḥ ||
english: Who can find happiness in the sight of this low person, whose wickedness is plain, who knows no restraint, whose base ways began long ago and spread, who has gained wealth by luck, and who hates virtue?
codex_problem: “In the sight of this low person” misreads गोचरगतैः: it refers to people who have come within his reach or sphere, not to people looking at him.
codex_sanskrit_says: It asks what happiness can be attained by those who come within the reach of this unrestrained base man, whose vile conduct is longstanding, who gained wealth by fate, and who hates virtue.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
मृगमीनसज्जनानां तृणजलसंतोषविहितवृत्तीनाम्।
लुब्धकधीवरपिशुना निष्कारणवैरिणो जगति ॥
iast:
mṛgamīnasajjanānāṃ tṛṇajalasaṃtoṣavihitavṛttīnām|
lubdhakadhīvarapiśunā niṣkāraṇavairiṇo jagati ||
english: Deer, fish and good people live content with grass, water and contentment; yet hunters, fishermen and slanderers are their enemies in the world without any cause.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
विपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः।
यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम् ॥
iast:
vipadi dhairyamathābhyudaye kṣamā sadasi vākpaṭutā yudhi vikramaḥ|
yaśasi cābhirucirvyasanaṃ śrutau prakṛtisiddhamidaṃ hi mahātmanām ||
english: Steadiness in adversity, forbearance in prosperity, eloquence in the assembly, valour in battle, a taste for good repute, and a passion for learning: this is the inborn nature of the great-souled.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
करे श्लाघ्यस्त्यागः शिरसि गुरुपादप्रणयिता मुखे सत्या वाणी विजयि भुजयोर्वीर्यमतुलम्।
हृदि स्वच्छा वृत्तिः श्रुतमधिगतैकव्रतफलं विनाऽप्यैश्वर्येण प्रकृतिमहतां मण्डनमिदम् ॥
iast:
kare ślāghyastyāgaḥ śirasi gurupādapraṇayitā mukhe satyā vāṇī vijayi bhujayorvīryamatulam|
hṛdi svacchā vṛttiḥ śrutamadhigataikavrataphalaṃ vinā'pyaiśvaryeṇa prakṛtimahatāṃ maṇḍanamidam ||
english: Praiseworthy giving in the hand, devotion to the teacher's feet on the head, truthful speech in the mouth, unequalled victorious strength in the arms, a clear disposition in the heart, learning in the ears: these adorn the naturally great, even without riches.
codex_problem: The English adds “in the ears,” which is absent from the supplied Sanskrit, and omits the qualification अधिगतैकव्रतफलम् attached to learning.
codex_sanskrit_says: The supplied text lists a pure disposition in the heart and learning described as the attained fruit of a single-minded vow or discipline; these adorn the naturally great even without riches.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
संतप्तायसि संस्थितस्य पयसो नामाऽपि न ज्ञायते मुक्ताकारतया तदेव नलिनीपत्रस्थितं राजते।
स्वात्यां सागरशुक्तिमध्यपतितं तन्मौक्तिकं जायते प्रायेणाधममध्यमोत्तमगुणः संसर्गतो जायते ॥
iast:
saṃtaptāyasi saṃsthitasya payaso nāmā'pi na jñāyate muktākāratayā tadeva nalinīpatrasthitaṃ rājate|
svātyāṃ sāgaraśuktimadhyapatitaṃ tanmauktikaṃ jāyate prāyeṇādhamamadhyamottamaguṇaḥ saṃsargato jāyate ||
english: On red-hot iron, a drop of water leaves not even a trace; on a lotus leaf, the same drop shines like a pearl; falling into a sea-shell at the right season, it becomes a pearl. As a rule, low, middling and high qualities come from the company one keeps.
codex_problem: “At the right season” replaces the specifically named Svāti with a generic reference to timing.
codex_sanskrit_says: The drop becomes a pearl when it falls into a sea-oyster during Svāti.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
यः प्रीणयेत्सुचरितैः पितरं स पुत्रो यद्भर्तुरेव हितमिच्छति तत्कलत्रम्।
तन्मित्रमापदि सुखे च समक्रियं य- देतत्त्रयं जगति पुण्यकृतो लभन्ते ॥
iast:
yaḥ prīṇayetsucaritaiḥ pitaraṃ sa putro yadbhartureva hitamicchati tatkalatram|
tanmitramāpadi sukhe ca samakriyaṃ ya- detattrayaṃ jagati puṇyakṛto labhante ||
english: A son is one who pleases his father by good conduct; a wife is one who wishes only for her husband's good; a friend is one who acts the same in trouble and in happiness. Those who have done good deeds find these three in the world.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
एको देवः केशवो वा शिवो वा ह्येकं मित्रं भूपतिर्वा यतिर्वा।
एको वासः पत्तने वा वने वा ह्येका भार्या सुन्दरी वा दरी वा ॥
iast:
eko devaḥ keśavo vā śivo vā hyekaṃ mitraṃ bhūpatirvā yatirvā|
eko vāsaḥ pattane vā vane vā hyekā bhāryā sundarī vā darī vā ||
english: One god, Keshava or Shiva; one friend, a king or an ascetic; one dwelling, in a city or a forest; one wife, a beautiful woman or a cave.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नम्रत्वेनोन्नमन्तः परगुणकथनैः स्वान्गुणान्ख्यापयन्तः स्वार्थान्सम्पादयन्तो विततपृथुतरारम्भयत्नाः परार्थे।
क्षान्त्यैवाऽऽक्षेपरूक्षाक्षरमुखरमुखान् दुर्मुखान्दूषयन्तः सन्तः साश्चर्यचर्या जगति बहुमताः कस्य नाभ्यर्चनीयाः ॥
iast:
namratvenonnamantaḥ paraguṇakathanaiḥ svānguṇānkhyāpayantaḥ svārthānsampādayanto vitatapṛthutarārambhayatnāḥ parārthe|
kṣāntyaivā''kṣeparūkṣākṣaramukharamukhān durmukhāndūṣayantaḥ santaḥ sāścaryacaryā jagati bahumatāḥ kasya nābhyarcanīyāḥ ||
english: Rising by humility, making their own virtues known by speaking of others' virtues, achieving their own aims by great efforts for others, and shaming harsh-tongued slanderers by forbearance alone: who would not honour the good, whose ways are a wonder in the world?
codex_problem: The word “by” makes great efforts for others sound like the means by which the good achieve their own aims. The Sanskrit juxtaposes their accomplishing their own aims with their extensive exertions for others, without making the latter a self-interested means.
codex_sanskrit_says: The good rise through humility, reveal their virtues by praising others, accomplish their own aims while undertaking extensive efforts for others, and shame harsh-mouthed detractors through patience alone.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम्।
अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्यायात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
iast:
nindantu nītinipuṇā yadi vā stuvantu lakṣmīḥ samāviśatu gacchatu vā yatheṣṭam|
adyaiva vā maraṇamastu yugāntare vā nyāyātpathaḥ pravicalanti padaṃ na dhīrāḥ ||
english: Let the experts in policy blame or praise; let fortune come or go as it pleases; let death come today or after an age: the steadfast do not stray a single step from the path of justice.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
भग्नाशस्य करण्डपीडिततनोर्म्लानेन्द्रियस्य क्षुधा कृत्वाऽऽखुर्विवरं स्वयं निपतितो नक्तं मुखे भोगिनः।
तृप्तस्तत्पिशितेन सत्वरमसौ तेनैव यातः पथा लोकाः पश्यत दैवमेव हि नृणां वृद्धौ क्षये कारणम् ॥
iast:
bhagnāśasya karaṇḍapīḍitatanormlānendriyasya kṣudhā kṛtvā''khurvivaraṃ svayaṃ nipatito naktaṃ mukhe bhoginaḥ|
tṛptastatpiśitena satvaramasau tenaiva yātaḥ pathā lokāḥ paśyata daivameva hi nṛṇāṃ vṛddhau kṣaye kāraṇam ||
english: A snake, hopeless, its body crushed in a basket, its senses fading with hunger: a rat gnawed a hole and fell into its mouth at night by itself. Satisfied by its flesh, the snake quickly escaped by that same path. People, see: fate alone is the cause of rise and fall for humans.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नेता यस्य बृहस्पतिः प्रहरणं वज्रं सुराः सैनिकाः स्वर्गो दुर्गमनुग्रहः किल हरेरैरावतो वारणः।
इत्यैश्वर्यबलान्वितोऽपि बलभिद्भग्नः परैः सङ्गरे तद्युक्तं ननु दैवमेव शरणं धिग्धिग्वृथा पौरुषम् ॥
iast:
netā yasya bṛhaspatiḥ praharaṇaṃ vajraṃ surāḥ sainikāḥ svargo durgamanugrahaḥ kila harerairāvato vāraṇaḥ|
ityaiśvaryabalānvito'pi balabhidbhagnaḥ paraiḥ saṅgare tadyuktaṃ nanu daivameva śaraṇaṃ dhigdhigvṛthā pauruṣam ||
english: His leader was Brihaspati, his weapon the thunderbolt, the gods his soldiers, heaven his fortress, Hari's favour his support, Airavata his elephant: yet even Indra, with all this power and strength, was defeated by enemies in battle. So fate alone is the refuge; shame, shame on useless human effort.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कर्मायत्तं फलं पुंसां बुद्धिः कर्मानुसारिणी।
तथाऽपि सुधिया भाव्यं सुविचार्यैव कुर्वता ॥
iast:
karmāyattaṃ phalaṃ puṃsāṃ buddhiḥ karmānusāriṇī|
tathā'pi sudhiyā bhāvyaṃ suvicāryaiva kurvatā ||
english: The fruits people reap depend on their actions, and the mind follows their actions. Even so, the wise should act only after careful thought.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
खल्वाटो दिवसेश्वरस्य किरणैः संतापितो मस्तके वाञ्छन्देशमनातपं विधिवशात्तालस्य मूलं गतः।
तत्राऽप्यस्य महाफलेन पतता भग्नं सशब्दं शिरः प्रायो गच्छति यत्र भाग्यरहितस्तत्रैव यान्त्यापदः ॥
iast:
khalvāṭo divaseśvarasya kiraṇaiḥ saṃtāpito mastake vāñchandeśamanātapaṃ vidhivaśāttālasya mūlaṃ gataḥ|
tatrā'pyasya mahāphalena patatā bhagnaṃ saśabdaṃ śiraḥ prāyo gacchati yatra bhāgyarahitastatraiva yāntyāpadaḥ ||
english: A bald man, his head scorched by the rays of the sun, seeking a shady spot, went by fate to the foot of a palm tree; there too, a great falling fruit broke his head with a crack. Usually, wherever the luckless go, misfortunes go too.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
गजभुजङ्गमयोरपि बन्धनं शशिदिवाकरयोर्ग्रहपीडनम्।
मतिमताञ्च विलोक्य दरिद्रतां विधिरहो ! बलवानिति मे मतिः ॥
iast:
gajabhujaṅgamayorapi bandhanaṃ śaśidivākarayorgrahapīḍanam|
matimatāñca vilokya daridratāṃ vidhiraho ! balavāniti me matiḥ ||
english: Seeing even elephants and snakes in bonds, the moon and sun troubled by eclipse, and the intelligent in poverty, my view is: ah, fate is strong.

why_listed: Codex disagrees; safety flags: fatalism, death
speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
सृजति तावदशेषगुणाकरं पुरुषरत्नमलङ्करणं भुवः।
तदपि तत्क्षणभङ्गि करोति चे- दहह ! कष्टमपण्डितता विधेः ॥
iast:
sṛjati tāvadaśeṣaguṇākaraṃ puruṣaratnamalaṅkaraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ|
tadapi tatkṣaṇabhaṅgi karoti ce- dahaha ! kaṣṭamapaṇḍitatā vidheḥ ||
english: Fate creates a jewel of a person, a mine of every virtue, an ornament to the earth, and then makes him perish in a moment. Alas, what a pity, the folly of fate!
codex_problem: The English turns the conditional cet (“if”) into a definite sequence and mistakes tad api (“even that”) for “and then.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Fate creates a jewel among men, a repository of every virtue and ornament of the earth; if it makes even that perish in an instant, alas for fate’s folly.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
पत्रं नैव यदा करीरविटपे दोषो वसन्तस्य किं-नोलूकोऽप्यवलोकते यदि दिवा सूर्यस्य किं दूषणम्।
धारा नैव पतन्ति चातकमुखे मेघस्य किं दूषणं यत्पूर्वं विधिना ललाटलिखितं तन्मार्जितुं कः क्षमः ॥
iast:
patraṃ naiva yadā karīraviṭape doṣo vasantasya kiṃ-nolūko'pyavalokate yadi divā sūryasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam|
dhārā naiva patanti cātakamukhe meghasya kiṃ dūṣaṇaṃ yatpūrvaṃ vidhinā lalāṭalikhitaṃ tanmārjituṃ kaḥ kṣamaḥ ||
english: If the karira bush has no leaves, is spring at fault? If the owl does not see by day, is it the sun's fault? If rain does not fall into the chataka's mouth, is it the cloud's fault? Who can wipe away what the Creator wrote on the forehead long ago?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नमस्यामो देवान्ननु हतविधेस्तेऽपि वशगा विधिर्वन्द्यः सोऽपि प्रतिनियतकर्मैकफलदः।
फलं कर्मायत्तं किममरगणैः किञ्च विधिना नमस्तत्कर्मभ्यो विधिरपि न येभ्यः प्रभवति ॥
iast:
namasyāmo devānnanu hatavidheste'pi vaśagā vidhirvandyaḥ so'pi pratiniyatakarmaikaphaladaḥ|
phalaṃ karmāyattaṃ kimamaragaṇaiḥ kiñca vidhinā namastatkarmabhyo vidhirapi na yebhyaḥ prabhavati ||
english: We bow to the gods; but they are under the power of wretched fate. Fate is to be revered; but it gives only the fixed fruit of actions. If the fruit depends on action, what use are the gods, and what use is fate? Salutations to those actions, over which even fate has no power.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
अपि च - ब्रह्मा येन कुलालवन्नियमितो ब्रह्माण्डभाण्डोदरे विष्णुर्येन दशावतारगहने क्षिप्तो महासंकटे।
रुद्रो येन कपालपाणिपुटके भिक्षाटनं कारितः सूर्यो भ्राम्यति नित्यमेव गगने तस्मै नमः कर्मणे ॥
iast:
api ca - brahmā yena kulālavanniyamito brahmāṇḍabhāṇḍodare viṣṇuryena daśāvatāragahane kṣipto mahāsaṃkaṭe|
rudro yena kapālapāṇipuṭake bhikṣāṭanaṃ kāritaḥ sūryo bhrāmyati nityameva gagane tasmai namaḥ karmaṇe ||
english: Moreover: by which Brahma is held like a potter within the pot of the universe, Vishnu is thrown into the great trouble of ten incarnations, Rudra is made to beg with a skull in his hand, and the sun wanders the sky every day: salutations to that karma.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नैवाकृतिः फलति नैव कुलं न शीलं विद्यापि नैव न च यत्नकृताऽपि सेवा।
भाग्यानि पूर्वतपसा खलु सञ्चितानि काले फलन्ति पुरुषस्य यथैव वृक्षाः ॥
iast:
naivākṛtiḥ phalati naiva kulaṃ na śīlaṃ vidyāpi naiva na ca yatnakṛtā'pi sevā|
bhāgyāni pūrvatapasā khalu sañcitāni kāle phalanti puruṣasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ ||
english: Neither appearance bears fruit, nor family, nor character, nor even learning, nor service done with effort. Only the fortunes stored up by past austerities bear fruit for a person in time, as trees do.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
वने रणे शत्रुजलाग्निमध्ये महार्णवे पर्वतमस्तके वा।
सुप्तं प्रमत्तं विषमस्थितं वा रक्षन्ति पुण्यानि पुरा कृतानि ॥
iast:
vane raṇe śatrujalāgnimadhye mahārṇave parvatamastake vā|
suptaṃ pramattaṃ viṣamasthitaṃ vā rakṣanti puṇyāni purā kṛtāni ||
english: In the forest, in battle, amid enemies, water and fire, on the great ocean or a mountain top, whether asleep, careless or in danger, the good deeds done before protect a person.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
मज्जत्वम्भसि यातु मेरुशिखरं शत्रूञ्जयत्वाहवे वाणिज्यं कृषिसेवनादिसकला विद्याः कलाः शिक्षताम्।
आकाशं विपुलं प्रयातु खगवत्कृत्वा प्रयत्नं महा- न्नाभाव्यं भवतीह कर्मवशतो भाव्यस्य नाशः कुतः ॥
iast:
majjatvambhasi yātu meruśikharaṃ śatrūñjayatvāhave vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣisevanādisakalā vidyāḥ kalāḥ śikṣatām|
ākāśaṃ vipulaṃ prayātu khagavatkṛtvā prayatnaṃ mahā- nnābhāvyaṃ bhavatīha karmavaśato bhāvyasya nāśaḥ kutaḥ ||
english: Let him dive into the water, go to the top of Meru, conquer enemies in battle, learn trade, farming, service and all the arts and sciences, fly through the wide sky like a bird with great effort: what is not to be will not happen here, through the power of karma, and how can what is to be be destroyed?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
भीमं वनं भवति तस्य पुरं प्रधानं सर्वे जनाः सुजनतामुपयान्ति तस्य।
कृत्स्ना च भूर्भवति सन्निधिरत्नपूर्णा यस्यास्ति पूर्वसुकृतं विपुलं नरस्य ॥
iast:
bhīmaṃ vanaṃ bhavati tasya puraṃ pradhānaṃ sarve janāḥ sujanatāmupayānti tasya|
kṛtsnā ca bhūrbhavati sannidhiratnapūrṇā yasyāsti pūrvasukṛtaṃ vipulaṃ narasya ||
english: For the person who has abundant past good deeds, a fearsome forest becomes a chief city, all people become good to him, and the whole earth becomes full of treasures and jewels.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
को लाभो गुणिसङ्गमः किमसुखं प्राज्ञेतरैः सङ्गतिः का हानिः समयच्युतिर्निपुणता का धर्मतत्त्वे रतिः।
कः शूरो विजितेन्द्रियः प्रियतमा काऽनुव्रता किं धनं विद्या किं सुखमप्रवासगमनं राज्यं किमाज्ञाफलम् ॥
iast:
ko lābho guṇisaṅgamaḥ kimasukhaṃ prājñetaraiḥ saṅgatiḥ kā hāniḥ samayacyutirnipuṇatā kā dharmatattve ratiḥ|
kaḥ śūro vijitendriyaḥ priyatamā kā'nuvratā kiṃ dhanaṃ vidyā kiṃ sukhamapravāsagamanaṃ rājyaṃ kimājñāphalam ||
english: What is gain? The company of the virtuous. What is unhappiness? Company with fools. What is loss? Missing the right moment. What is skill? Delight in the truth of dharma. Who is a hero? One who has mastered the senses. Who is dearest? A faithful partner. What is wealth? Learning. What is happiness? Not having to live away from home. What is a kingdom? Having one's word obeyed.
codex_problem: “A faithful partner” modernizes away the explicitly feminine reference and the traditional relationship expressed by anuvratā.
codex_sanskrit_says: Asked who is the dearest woman or wife, the verse answers: one who is devoted or faithful to her husband.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कान्ताकटाक्षविशखा न लुनन्ति यस्य चित्तं न निर्दहति कोपकृशानुतापः।
कर्षन्ति भूरिविषयाश्च न लोभपाशै- र्लोकत्रयं जयति कृत्स्नमिदं स धीरः ॥
iast:
kāntākaṭākṣaviśakhā na lunanti yasya cittaṃ na nirdahati kopakṛśānutāpaḥ|
karṣanti bhūriviṣayāśca na lobhapāśai- rlokatrayaṃ jayati kṛtsnamidaṃ sa dhīraḥ ||
english: Whose mind is not pierced by the arrows of a lover's glances, not burnt by the fire of anger, and not dragged by the many objects of the senses with the nooses of greed: that steadfast person conquers all three worlds.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
एकेनापि हि शूरेण पादाक्रान्तं महीतलम्।
क्रियते भास्करेणेव स्फारस्फुरिततेजसा ॥
iast:
ekenāpi hi śūreṇa pādākrāntaṃ mahītalam|
kriyate bhāskareṇeva sphārasphuritatejasā ||
english: Even by one brave person the whole earth is brought under foot, as by the sun with its blazing brilliance.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
लज्जागुणौघजननीं जननीमिव स्वा-मत्यन्तशुद्धहृदयामनुवर्त्तमानाम्।
तेजस्विनः सुखमसूनपि संत्यजन्ति सत्यव्रतव्यसनिनो न पुनः प्रतिज्ञाम् ॥
iast:
lajjāguṇaughajananīṃ jananīmiva svā-matyantaśuddhahṛdayāmanuvarttamānām|
tejasvinaḥ sukhamasūnapi saṃtyajanti satyavratavyasanino na punaḥ pratijñām ||
english: Those of spirit, devoted to the vow of truth, will gladly give up even their life, but never their promise, which, like their own mother, is pure of heart, gives birth to a flood of virtues such as modesty, and always follows them.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विपरीततरश्च त्वं भागधेये न संमतः ।
अर्चिषां प्रक्षयाच्चैव धर्मात्मा धर्मकोविदः ॥
iast:
viparītataraśca tvaṃ bhāgadheye na saṃmataḥ |
arciṣāṃ prakṣayāccaiva dharmātmā dharmakovidaḥ ||
english: You are quite the opposite, not counted worthy of a share, though righteous and learned in dharma, because of the loss of your eyesight.
codex_problem: The English reverses bhāgadheye na saṃmataḥ: it does not say that Dhritarashtra is considered unworthy of a share. It also wrongly makes “righteous and learned in dharma” describe Dhritarashtra rather than Yudhishthira.
codex_sanskrit_says: Dhritarashtra has acted quite oppositely and has not consented to Yudhishthira’s rightful share; Yudhishthira is righteous and versed in dharma. The verse also refers to the loss of light or eyesight.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
दुर्योधने सौबले च कर्णे दुःशासने तथा ।
एतेष्वैश्वर्यमाधाय कथं त्वं भूतिमिच्छसि ॥
iast:
duryodhane saubale ca karṇe duḥśāsane tathā |
eteṣvaiśvaryamādhāya kathaṃ tvaṃ bhūtimicchasi ||
english: Having placed your sovereignty in Duryodhana, Shakuni, Karna and Duhshasana, how can you hope for prosperity?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एकस्मात्वृक्षाद्यज्ञपत्राणि राजन्
स्रुक्च द्रौणी पेठनीपीडने च ।
एतस्माद्राजन्ब्रुवतो मे निबोध
एकस्माद्वै जायतेऽसच्च सच्च ॥
iast:
ekasmātvṛkṣādyajñapatrāṇi rājan
srukca drauṇī peṭhanīpīḍane ca |
etasmādrājanbruvato me nibodha
ekasmādvai jāyate'sacca sacca ||
english: From one tree, king, come the vessels for sacrifice, the ladle, the trough and the press. From this, king, learn from me as I speak: from one source arise both the bad and the good.
codex_problem: The English collapses or omits one of the final two implements: peṭhanī and pīḍana are separately named, but only one “press” is given.
codex_sanskrit_says: From one tree come the sacrificial vessels, the ladle, the trough, the peṭhanī and the pīḍana; likewise, both bad and good arise from one source.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्य संसारिणी प्रज्ञा धर्मार्थावनुवर्तते ।
कामादर्थं वृणीते यः स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
yasya saṃsāriṇī prajñā dharmārthāvanuvartate |
kāmādarthaṃ vṛṇīte yaḥ sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One whose practical understanding follows dharma and true benefit, and who chooses real benefit over pleasure, is called wise.
codex_problem: “True benefit” and “real benefit” reinterpret artha by adding the qualification “true/real.” Here artha is advantage, material interest or profit, contrasted with kāma.
codex_sanskrit_says: One whose practical intelligence follows dharma and artha, and who chooses artha rather than kāma, is called wise.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
क्षिप्रं विजानाति चिरं शृणोति
विज्ञाय चार्थं भजते न कामात् ।
नासम्पृष्टो व्यौपयुङ्क्ते परार्थे
तत्प्रज्ञानं प्रथमं पण्डितस्य ॥
iast:
kṣipraṃ vijānāti ciraṃ śṛṇoti
vijñāya cārthaṃ bhajate na kāmāt |
nāsampṛṣṭo vyaupayuṅkte parārthe
tatprajñānaṃ prathamaṃ paṇḍitasya ||
english: Understanding quickly, listening long, acting on a matter only after grasping it and not out of desire, not offering opinions on others' affairs unasked: this is the first mark of the wise.
codex_problem: “Not offering opinions” is too narrow and introduces speech that the Sanskrit does not specify. The verb means not engaging or interfering in another person’s affairs without being asked.
codex_sanskrit_says: He understands quickly, listens at length, pursues a matter after understanding it rather than from desire, and does not engage in another’s affair unasked.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थं महान्तमासद्य विद्यामैश्वर्यमेव च ।
विचरत्यसमुन्नद्धो यस्य पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
arthaṃ mahāntamāsadya vidyāmaiśvaryameva ca |
vicaratyasamunnaddho yasya paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who, having gained great wealth, learning or power, moves about without arrogance is called wise.
codex_problem: The English changes the Sanskrit’s conjunction to an alternative: the verse says wealth, learning and power, not wealth, learning or power.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who, having attained great wealth, learning and power, conducts himself without arrogance is called wise.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्वमर्थं यः परित्यज्य परार्थमनुतिष्ठति ।
मिथ्या चरति मित्रार्थे यश्च मूढः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
svamarthaṃ yaḥ parityajya parārthamanutiṣṭhati |
mithyā carati mitrārthe yaśca mūḍhaḥ sa ucyate ||
english: One who gives up their own business to pursue another's, and who behaves falsely in matters concerning friends, is called a fool.
codex_problem: Mitrārthe means “for a friend’s sake” or “in a friend’s interest,” not merely “in matters concerning friends.” The English loses the stated purpose of the false conduct.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who abandons his own interest to pursue another’s, and who acts falsely for a friend’s sake, is called a fool.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अकामां कामयति यः कामयानां परित्यजेत् ।
बलवन्तं च यो द्वेष्टि तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
akāmāṃ kāmayati yaḥ kāmayānāṃ parityajet |
balavantaṃ ca yo dveṣṭi tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who desires those who do not desire them and rejects those who do, and who hates the powerful, they call a fool.
codex_problem: The first object, akāmām, is specifically a singular feminine person—a woman who does not desire him. Rendering it as the gender-neutral plural “those” removes that explicit sense.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who desires a woman who does not desire him, abandons those who desire him, and hates a powerful person is called foolish-minded.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनाहूतः प्रविशति अपृष्टो बहु भाषते ।
विश्वसत्यप्रमत्तेषु मूढ चेता नराधमः ॥
iast:
anāhūtaḥ praviśati apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate |
viśvasatyapramatteṣu mūḍha cetā narādhamaḥ ||
english: Entering uninvited, talking much without being asked, and trusting the untrustworthy: such a person is a fool and the lowest of people.
codex_problem: The supplied Sanskrit has apramatteṣu, “among vigilant or careful people,” not “the untrustworthy.” The English appears to follow a different or emended reading.
codex_sanskrit_says: He enters uninvited, speaks at length without being asked, and places trust in vigilant or careful people; such a person is foolish-minded and the lowest of men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आत्मनो बलमाज्ञाय धर्मार्थपरिवर्जितम् ।
अलभ्यमिच्छन्नैष्कर्म्यान्मूढ बुद्धिरिहोच्यते ॥
iast:
ātmano balamājñāya dharmārthaparivarjitam |
alabhyamicchannaiṣkarmyānmūḍha buddhirihocyate ||
english: Not knowing their own strength, wanting what cannot be had without dharma or real benefit and without effort: such a person is called a fool.
codex_problem: The supplied Sanskrit says ājñāya, “having known or assessed,” whereas the English says “not knowing,” which reverses the meaning. It also does not say that the desired object “cannot be had without dharma or real benefit.”
codex_sanskrit_says: It speaks of having assessed one’s own strength, of the absence of dharma and artha, and of desiring the unattainable through inactivity; such a person is called foolish-minded.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एकं हन्यान्न वाहन्यादिषुर्मुक्तो धनुष्मता ।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतोत्सृष्टा हन्याद्राष्ट्रं सराजकम् ॥
iast:
ekaṃ hanyānna vāhanyādiṣurmukto dhanuṣmatā |
buddhirbuddhimatotsṛṣṭā hanyādrāṣṭraṃ sarājakam ||
english: An arrow shot by an archer may kill one person or none; but a plan let loose by a clever mind can destroy a kingdom together with its king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अतृणे पतितो वह्निः स्वयमेवोपशाम्यति ।
अक्षमावान्परं दोषैरात्मान्ं चैव योजयेत् ॥
iast:
atṛṇe patito vahniḥ svayamevopaśāmyati |
akṣamāvānparaṃ doṣairātmānṃ caiva yojayet ||
english: Fire falling where there is no grass goes out by itself; but one without forgiveness entangles others, and themselves too, in faults.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ ग्रसते भूमिः सर्पो बिलशयानिव ।
राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvimau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayāniva |
rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam ||
english: The earth swallows these two as a snake swallows creatures lying in their holes: a king who does not resist, and a brahmin who never leaves home.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र परप्रत्यय कारिणौ ।
स्त्रियः कामित कामिन्यो लोकः पूजित पूजकः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra parapratyaya kāriṇau |
striyaḥ kāmita kāminyo lokaḥ pūjita pūjakaḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, act on the belief of others: women who desire those desired by others, and people who honour whoever is honoured.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वावेव न विराजेते विपरीतेन कर्मणा ।
गृहस्थश्च निरारंभः कार्यवांश्चैव भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
dvāveva na virājete viparītena karmaṇā |
gṛhasthaśca nirāraṃbhaḥ kāryavāṃścaiva bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: These two do not shine, acting against their role: a householder without enterprise, and a mendicant busy with worldly affairs.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वावंभसि निवेष्टव्यौ गले बद्ध्वा दृढं शिलाम् ।
धनवन्तमदातारं दरिद्रं चातपस्विनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvaṃbhasi niveṣṭavyau gale baddhvā dṛḍhaṃ śilām |
dhanavantamadātāraṃ daridraṃ cātapasvinam ||
english: These two should be thrown into the water with a stone tied firmly to the neck: a rich person who does not give, and a poor person who does not practise austerity.
