speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र सुर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ ।
परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra suryamaṇḍalabhedinau |
parivrāḍyogayuktaśca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, pierce the disc of the sun: a wandering ascetic joined in yoga, and one slain in battle while facing the enemy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्रय एवाधना राजन्भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः ।
यत्ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम् ॥
iast:
traya evādhanā rājanbhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ |
yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam ||
english: Three own no wealth, king: a wife, a slave and a son. Whatever they earn belongs to the one they belong to.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हरणं च परस्वानां परदाराभिमर्शनम् ।
सुहृदश्च परित्यागस्त्रयो दोषा क्षयावहः ॥
iast:
haraṇaṃ ca parasvānāṃ paradārābhimarśanam |
suhṛdaśca parityāgastrayo doṣā kṣayāvahaḥ ||
english: Taking what belongs to others, assaulting another's wife and abandoning a friend: these three faults bring ruin.
codex_problem: “Assaulting” makes the act specifically violent, whereas par­adārābhimarśanam denotes touching or violating another man's wife—illicit sexual involvement—without necessarily implying force.
codex_sanskrit_says: Taking others' property, violating another's wife, and abandoning a friend are three faults that bring ruin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वरप्रदानं राज्यां च पुत्रजन्म च भारत ।
शत्रोश्च मोक्षणं कृच्छ्रात्त्रीणि चैकं च तत्समम् ॥
iast:
varapradānaṃ rājyāṃ ca putrajanma ca bhārata |
śatrośca mokṣaṇaṃ kṛcchrāttrīṇi caikaṃ ca tatsamam ||
english: Receiving a boon, gaining a kingdom and the birth of a son, Bharata: these three, and a fourth, rescuing an enemy from distress, are equal.
codex_problem: Varapradānam means granting or bestowing a boon, not receiving one.
codex_sanskrit_says: Granting a boon, a kingdom, and the birth of a son—these three are equal to the single act of rescuing an enemy from distress.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता ।
निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता ॥
iast:
ṣaḍdoṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtimicchatā |
nidrā tandrī bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratā ||
english: Six faults should be given up here by a person who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
codex_problem: The qualification “too much” is not present in the Sanskrit; nidrā simply says “sleep.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The six faults to be abandoned by one seeking prosperity are sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness, and procrastination.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अरक्षितारं राजानं भार्यां चाप्रिय वादिनीम् ।
ग्रामकारं च गोपालं वनकामं च नापितम् ॥
iast:
arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpriya vādinīm |
grāmakāraṃ ca gopālaṃ vanakāmaṃ ca nāpitam ||
english: a king who does not protect, a wife who speaks unkindly, a cowherd who wants to live in the village, and a barber who wants to live in the forest.
codex_problem: The supplied Sanskrit reads grāmakāram, not grāmakāmam; therefore it does not say that the cowherd “wants to live in the village.” The English reflects a likely emendation of the text rather than the text provided.
codex_sanskrit_says: As supplied, the verse lists a king who does not protect, an unpleasant-speaking wife, a grāmakāra cowherd, and a barber who desires the forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थागमो नित्यमरोगिता च
प्रिया च भार्या प्रियवादिनी च ।
वश्यश्च पुत्रोऽर्थकरी च विद्या
षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन् ॥
iast:
arthāgamo nityamarogitā ca
priyā ca bhāryā priyavādinī ca |
vaśyaśca putro'rthakarī ca vidyā
ṣaṭ jīvalokasya sukhāni rājan ||
english: A steady income, constant good health, a beloved and sweet-spoken wife, an obedient son and knowledge that earns a living: these, king, are the six joys of the world of the living.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रमदाः कामयानेषु यजमानेषु याजकाः ।
राजा विवदमानेषु नित्यं मूर्खेषु पण्डिताः ॥
iast:
pramadāḥ kāmayāneṣu yajamāneṣu yājakāḥ |
rājā vivadamāneṣu nityaṃ mūrkheṣu paṇḍitāḥ ||
english: women off the lustful, priests off those who sacrifice, the king off those who quarrel, and the learned always off fools.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडिमानि विनश्यन्ति मुहूर्तमनवेक्षणात् ।
गावः सेवा कृषिर्भार्या विद्या वृषलसंगतिः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍimāni vinaśyanti muhūrtamanavekṣaṇāt |
gāvaḥ sevā kṛṣirbhāryā vidyā vṛṣalasaṃgatiḥ ||
english: These six are ruined by a moment's neglect: cows, service, farming, a wife, learning and company with a shudra.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्त्रियोऽक्षा मृगया पानं वाक्पारुष्यं च पञ्चमम् ।
महच्च दण्डपारुष्यमर्थदूषणमेव च ॥
iast:
striyo'kṣā mṛgayā pānaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ ca pañcamam |
mahacca daṇḍapāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇameva ca ||
english: women, dice, hunting, drinking, harsh speech as the fifth, great harshness in punishment, and misuse of wealth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अष्टौ पूर्वनिमित्तानि नरस्य विनशिष्यतः ।
ब्राह्मणान्प्रथमं द्वेष्टि ब्राह्मणैश्च विरुध्यते ॥
iast:
aṣṭau pūrvanimittāni narasya vinaśiṣyataḥ |
brāhmaṇānprathamaṃ dveṣṭi brāhmaṇaiśca virudhyate ||
english: There are eight signs of a man about to be destroyed: first, he hates brahmins and is at odds with brahmins;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मण स्वानि चादत्ते ब्राह्मणांश्च जिघांसति ।
रमते निन्दया चैषां प्रशंसां नाभिनन्दति ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇa svāni cādatte brāhmaṇāṃśca jighāṃsati |
ramate nindayā caiṣāṃ praśaṃsāṃ nābhinandati ||
english: he takes brahmins' property and wishes to kill brahmins; he delights in blaming them and does not welcome their praise;
codex_problem: “Their praise” naturally suggests praise given by the brahmins, whereas the Sanskrit means praise of the brahmins, contrasting with their censure.
codex_sanskrit_says: He delights in censuring the brahmins and does not rejoice when they are praised.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नैतान्स्मरति कृत्येषु याचितश्चाभ्यसूयति ।
एतान्दोषान्नरः प्राज्ञो बुद्ध्या बुद्ध्वा विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
naitānsmarati kṛtyeṣu yācitaścābhyasūyati |
etāndoṣānnaraḥ prājño buddhyā buddhvā vivarjayet ||
english: he does not remember them in his rites, and resents them when asked. A wise person, understanding these faults, should avoid them.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं
नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रतीतः ।
दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं
न कत्थते सत्पुरुषार्य शीलः ॥
iast:
na sve sukhe vai kurute praharṣaṃ
nānyasya duḥkhe bhavati pratītaḥ |
dattvā na paścātkurute'nutāpaṃ
na katthate satpuruṣārya śīlaḥ ||
english: One who does not exult in his own happiness, does not rejoice at another's sorrow, does not regret having given, and does not boast: that is a good person of noble conduct.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
समैर्विवाहं कुरुते न हीनैः
समैः सख्यं व्यवहारं कथाश्च ।
गुणैर्विशिष्टांश्च पुरो दधाति
विपश्चितस्तस्य नयाः सुनीताः ॥
iast:
samairvivāhaṃ kurute na hīnaiḥ
samaiḥ sakhyaṃ vyavahāraṃ kathāśca |
guṇairviśiṣṭāṃśca puro dadhāti
vipaścitastasya nayāḥ sunītāḥ ||
english: One who marries among equals and not among inferiors, who makes friends, does business and converses with equals, and puts those of superior qualities first: that wise person's policies are well guided.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वने जाताः शापदग्धस्य राज्ञः
पाण्डोः पुत्राः पञ्च पञ्चेन्द्र कल्पाः ।
त्वयैव बाला वर्धिताः शिक्षिताश्च
तवादेशं पालयन्त्याम्बिकेय ॥
iast:
vane jātāḥ śāpadagdhasya rājñaḥ
pāṇḍoḥ putrāḥ pañca pañcendra kalpāḥ |
tvayaiva bālā vardhitāḥ śikṣitāśca
tavādeśaṃ pālayantyāmbikeya ||
english: Born in the forest to King Pandu, who was burnt by a curse, the five sons of Pandu, like five Indras, were raised and taught by you as boys, and they follow your command, son of Ambika.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
त्वं मां यथावद्विदुर प्रशाधि
प्रज्ञा पूर्वं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ।
यन्मन्यसे पथ्यमदीनसत्त्व
श्रेयः करं ब्रूहि तद्वै कुरूणाम् ॥
iast:
tvaṃ māṃ yathāvadvidura praśādhi
prajñā pūrvaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ |
yanmanyase pathyamadīnasattva
śreyaḥ karaṃ brūhi tadvai kurūṇām ||
english: Instruct me properly, Vidura, about everything in Ajatashatru's mind. Whatever you think beneficial, you of undaunted spirit, tell me what will bring good to the Kurus.
codex_problem: “Everything in Ajatashatru’s mind” is more specific than the Sanskrit. Here prajñāpūrvam means wisely or with understanding; the verse asks for instruction concerning Ajatashatru, not specifically a report of his thoughts.
codex_sanskrit_says: Instruct me correctly and wisely concerning everything about Ajatashatru; tell me whatever you consider beneficial and conducive to the welfare of the Kurus.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
पापाशङ्गी पापमेव नौपश्यन्
पृच्छामि त्वां व्याकुलेनात्मनाहम् ।
कवे तन्मे ब्रूहि सर्वं यथावन्
मनीषितं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ॥
iast:
pāpāśaṅgī pāpameva naupaśyan
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vyākulenātmanāham |
kave tanme brūhi sarvaṃ yathāvan
manīṣitaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ ||
english: Fearing wrong, I see nothing but wrong; I ask you with a troubled mind. Seer, tell me everything truly that Ajatashatru intends.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनुबन्धं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य विपाकांश्चैव कर्मणाम् ।
उत्थानमात्मनश्चैव धीरः कुर्वीत वा न वा ॥
iast:
anubandhaṃ ca samprekṣya vipākāṃścaiva karmaṇām |
utthānamātmanaścaiva dhīraḥ kurvīta vā na vā ||
english: Considering the consequences and the results of actions, and also one's own resources, the steady person should act or not act.
codex_problem: “One's own resources” mistranslates utthānam ātmanaḥ, which refers to one's own exertion, initiative, or capacity for effort.
codex_sanskrit_says: After considering the consequences and results of actions, as well as one's own capacity for exertion, the steady person should act or refrain from acting.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्त्वेतानि प्रमाणानि यथोक्तान्यनुपश्यति ।
युक्तो धर्मार्थयोर्ज्ञाने स राज्यमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
yastvetāni pramāṇāni yathoktānyanupaśyati |
yukto dharmārthayorjñāne sa rājyamadhigacchati ||
english: But one who observes these measures as described, and is versed in knowledge of dharma and true benefit, gains the kingdom.
codex_problem: “True benefit” is an interpretive and misleading rendering of artha, and “true” is not present in the Sanskrit.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who observes these measures as described and possesses knowledge of dharma and artha gains the kingdom.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पुष्पं पुष्पं विचिन्वीत मूलच्छेदं न कारयेत् ।
मालाकार इवारामे न यथाङ्गारकारकः ॥
iast:
puṣpaṃ puṣpaṃ vicinvīta mūlacchedaṃ na kārayet |
mālākāra ivārāme na yathāṅgārakārakaḥ ||
english: Gather flower by flower and do not cut down the roots, like a gardener in a garden, not like a charcoal-burner.
codex_problem: Mālākāra means a garland-maker or flower-gatherer, not a gardener.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should gather flower after flower without cutting the roots, like a garland-maker in a garden and not like a charcoal-burner.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
य एव यत्नः क्रियते प्रर राष्ट्रावमर्दने ।
स एव यत्नः कर्तव्यः स्वराष्ट्र परिपालने ॥
iast:
ya eva yatnaḥ kriyate prara rāṣṭrāvamardane |
sa eva yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ svarāṣṭra paripālane ||
english: The same effort that is made to crush another's kingdom should be made to protect one's own.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अप्युन्मत्तात्प्रलपतो बालाच्च परिसर्पतः ।
सर्वतः सारमादद्यादश्मभ्य इव काञ्चनम् ॥
iast:
apyunmattātpralapato bālācca parisarpataḥ |
sarvataḥ sāramādadyādaśmabhya iva kāñcanam ||
english: One should take what is valuable from everywhere, even from the ravings of a madman or the prattle of a child, as gold from stones.
codex_problem: The Sanskrit describes a child crawling or wandering about, not the child's “prattle.” The English adds speech and restricts the source of what may be valuable.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should take what is valuable from everywhere—even from a babbling madman or a child crawling about—as gold is taken from stones.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गन्धेन गावः पश्यन्ति वेदैः पश्यन्ति ब्राह्मणाः ।
चारैः पश्यन्ति राजानश्चक्षुर्भ्यामितरे जनाः ॥
iast:
gandhena gāvaḥ paśyanti vedaiḥ paśyanti brāhmaṇāḥ |
cāraiḥ paśyanti rājānaścakṣurbhyāmitare janāḥ ||
english: Cows see by smell, brahmins see by the Vedas, kings see through spies, and other people see with their eyes.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पर्जन्यनाथाः पशवो राजानो मित्र बान्धवाः ।
पतयो बान्धवाः स्त्रीणां ब्राह्मणा वेद बान्धवाः ॥
iast:
parjanyanāthāḥ paśavo rājāno mitra bāndhavāḥ |
patayo bāndhavāḥ strīṇāṃ brāhmaṇā veda bāndhavāḥ ||
english: Animals have the rain cloud as protector, kings have their ministers as kin, women have their husbands as kin, and brahmins have the Vedas as kin.
codex_problem: Mitra means friends or allies, not ministers.
codex_sanskrit_says: Animals have the rain cloud as protector, kings have friends as kin, women have their husbands as kin, and brahmins have the Veda as kin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
मानेन रक्ष्यते धान्यमश्वान्रक्ष्यत्यनुक्रमः ।
अभीक्ष्णदर्शनाद्गावः स्त्रियो रक्ष्याः कुचेलतः ॥
iast:
mānena rakṣyate dhānyamaśvānrakṣyatyanukramaḥ |
abhīkṣṇadarśanādgāvaḥ striyo rakṣyāḥ kucelataḥ ||
english: Grain is protected by measuring, horses by training, cows by frequent watching, and women are to be protected by plain clothes.
codex_problem: “Plain clothes” softens kucela, which denotes bad, shabby, or dirty clothing.
codex_sanskrit_says: Grain is protected by measuring, horses by regular exercise or training, cows by frequent inspection, and women are to be protected by shabby clothing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न कुलं वृत्ति हीनस्य प्रमाणमिति मे मतिः ।
अन्त्येष्वपि हि जातानां वृत्तमेव विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
na kulaṃ vṛtti hīnasya pramāṇamiti me matiḥ |
antyeṣvapi hi jātānāṃ vṛttameva viśiṣyate ||
english: Family is no measure of one who lacks good conduct; that is my view. Even among those born lowest, conduct alone is what excels.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अकार्य करणाद्भीतः कार्याणां च विवर्जनात् ।
अकाले मन्त्रभेदाच्च येन माद्येन्न तत्पिबेत् ॥
iast:
akārya karaṇādbhītaḥ kāryāṇāṃ ca vivarjanāt |
akāle mantrabhedācca yena mādyenna tatpibet ||
english: Fearing wrong action, neglect of what should be done, and revealing counsel at the wrong time, one should not drink anything that intoxicates.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विद्यामदो धनमदस्तृतीयोऽभिजनो मदः ।
एते मदावलिप्तानामेत एव सतां दमाः ॥
iast:
vidyāmado dhanamadastṛtīyo'bhijano madaḥ |
ete madāvaliptānāmeta eva satāṃ damāḥ ||
english: Pride of learning, pride of wealth and, third, pride of family: these are intoxications for the arrogant, and these same things are restraints for the good.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
शीलं प्रधानं पुरुषे तद्यस्येह प्रणश्यति ।
न तस्य जीवितेनार्थो न धनेन न बन्धुभिः ॥
iast:
śīlaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣe tadyasyeha praṇaśyati |
na tasya jīvitenārtho na dhanena na bandhubhiḥ ||
english: Character is foremost in a person; for one who loses it here, there is no use in life, nor wealth, nor kin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आढ्यानां मांसपरमं मध्यानां गोरसोत्तरम् ।
लवणोत्तरं दरिद्राणां भोजनं भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
āḍhyānāṃ māṃsaparamaṃ madhyānāṃ gorasottaram |
lavaṇottaraṃ daridrāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ bharatarṣabha ||
english: The food of the rich is mainly meat, of the middling mainly milk products, and of the poor mainly salt, best of the Bharatas.
codex_problem: Parama and uttara describe what is foremost or best in each group's food, not what constitutes most of it. “Mainly” changes quality or preference into quantity.
codex_sanskrit_says: For the rich, meat is foremost; for those of middling means, milk products are foremost; and in the food of the poor, salt is foremost, O best of the Bharatas.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अवृत्तिर्भयमन्त्यानां मध्यानां मरणाद्भयम् ।
उत्तमानां तु मर्त्यानामवमानात्परं भयम् ॥
iast:
avṛttirbhayamantyānāṃ madhyānāṃ maraṇādbhayam |
uttamānāṃ tu martyānāmavamānātparaṃ bhayam ||
english: The lowest fear having no livelihood, the middling fear death, but the best of mortals fear dishonour most of all.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविजित्य य आत्मानममात्यान्विजिगीषते ।
अमित्रान्वाजितामात्यः सोऽवशः परिहीयते ॥
iast:
avijitya ya ātmānamamātyānvijigīṣate |
amitrānvājitāmātyaḥ so'vaśaḥ parihīyate ||
english: One who, without conquering himself, seeks to conquer his ministers and enemies, is overcome and helpless, and falls.
codex_problem: The English changes “ministers or enemies” to “ministers and enemies” and omits the repeated point that his ministers remain unconquered, replacing it with the unsupported phrase “is overcome.”
codex_sanskrit_says: One who, without conquering himself, seeks to conquer his ministers or his enemies, while his ministers remain unconquered, helplessly comes to ruin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धर्मार्थौ यः परित्यज्य स्यादिन्द्रियवशानुगः ।
श्रीप्राणधनदारेभ्य क्षिप्रं स परिहीयते ॥
iast:
dharmārthau yaḥ parityajya syādindriyavaśānugaḥ |
śrīprāṇadhanadārebhya kṣipraṃ sa parihīyate ||
english: One who abandons dharma and true benefit and follows the lead of the senses quickly loses fortune, life, wealth and spouse.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थानामीश्वरो यः स्यादिन्द्रियाणामनीश्वरः ।
इन्द्रियाणामनैश्वर्यादैश्वर्याद्भ्रश्यते हि सः ॥
iast:
arthānāmīśvaro yaḥ syādindriyāṇāmanīśvaraḥ |
indriyāṇāmanaiśvaryādaiśvaryādbhraśyate hi saḥ ||
english: One who is master of wealth but not master of the senses falls from mastery because of not mastering the senses.
codex_problem: The final “mastery” is too abstract: aiśvarya here is the wealth, power, or prosperity from which the person falls, not merely mastery itself.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who is master of wealth but not of his senses falls from his wealth or power because he lacks mastery over the senses.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आत्मनात्मानमन्विच्छेन्मनो बुद्धीन्द्रियैर्यतैः ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
iast:
ātmanātmānamanvicchenmano buddhīndriyairyataiḥ |
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
english: One should seek the self by the self, with mind, intellect and senses restrained; for the self alone is the self's friend, and the self alone is the self's enemy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
दृश्यन्ते हि दुरात्मानो वध्यमानाः स्वकर्म भिः ।
इन्द्रियाणामनीशत्वाद्राजानो राज्यविभ्रमैः ॥
iast:
dṛśyante hi durātmāno vadhyamānāḥ svakarma bhiḥ |
indriyāṇāmanīśatvādrājāno rājyavibhramaiḥ ||
english: The wicked are seen being destroyed by their own deeds, and kings by the loss of their kingdoms, through not being masters of their senses.
codex_problem: The English incorrectly separates “the wicked” and “kings” into two groups and mistranslates rājyavibhramaiḥ as “the loss of their kingdoms.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Wicked kings are seen being destroyed by their own deeds, through their failure to master their senses and through the errors or delusions of kingship.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
निजानुत्पततः शत्रून्पञ्च पञ्च प्रयोजनान् ।
यो मोहान्न निघृह्णाति तमापद्ग्रसते नरम् ॥
iast:
nijānutpatataḥ śatrūnpañca pañca prayojanān |
yo mohānna nighṛhṇāti tamāpadgrasate naram ||
english: One who, through delusion, does not restrain the five enemies rising within, each with its five aims, is swallowed by misfortune.
codex_problem: “Each with its five aims” incorrectly suggests that every one of the five enemies has five aims. The verse refers collectively to five inner enemies associated with five objects or purposes.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who through delusion does not restrain the five enemies arising within, whose objects or purposes are five, is swallowed by misfortune.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आत्मज्ञानमनायासस्तितिक्षा धर्मनित्यता ।
वाक्चैव गुप्ता दानं च नैतान्यन्त्येषु भारत ॥
iast:
ātmajñānamanāyāsastitikṣā dharmanityatā |
vākcaiva guptā dānaṃ ca naitānyantyeṣu bhārata ||
english: Self-knowledge, calm, endurance, constancy in dharma, guarded speech and generosity: these are not found among the lowest, Bharata.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आक्रोश परिवादाभ्यां विहिंसन्त्यबुधा बुधान् ।
वक्ता पापमुपादत्ते क्षममाणो विमुच्यते ॥
iast:
ākrośa parivādābhyāṃ vihiṃsantyabudhā budhān |
vaktā pāpamupādatte kṣamamāṇo vimucyate ||
english: The foolish hurt the wise with abuse and slander; the speaker takes on the sin, and the one who forgives is released.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां राज्ञां दण्डविधिर्बलम् ।
शुश्रूषा तु बलं स्त्रीणां क्षमागुणवतां बलम् ॥
iast:
hiṃsā balamasādhūnāṃ rājñāṃ daṇḍavidhirbalam |
śuśrūṣā tu balaṃ strīṇāṃ kṣamāguṇavatāṃ balam ||
english: Violence is the strength of the wicked; punishment is the strength of kings; service is the strength of women; forgiveness is the strength of the virtuous.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्मै देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति पुरुषाय पराभवम् ।
बुद्धिं तस्यापकर्षन्ति सोऽपाचीनानि पश्यति ॥
iast:
yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam |
buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti so'pācīnāni paśyati ||
english: When the gods intend defeat for a person, they first take away his understanding, and he sees things the wrong way round.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सर्वतीर्थेषु वा स्नानं सर्वभूतेषु चार्जवम् ।
उभे एते समे स्यातामार्जवं वा विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
sarvatīrtheṣu vā snānaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cārjavam |
ubhe ete same syātāmārjavaṃ vā viśiṣyate ||
english: Bathing at all the holy places, and straightforwardness towards all beings: these two may be equal, or straightforwardness may be greater.

speaker: Keshini
devanagari:
किं ब्राह्मणाः स्विच्छ्रेयांसो दितिजाः स्विद्विरोचन ।
अथ केन स्म पर्यङ्कं सुधन्वा नाधिरोहति ॥
iast:
kiṃ brāhmaṇāḥ svicchreyāṃso ditijāḥ svidvirocana |
atha kena sma paryaṅkaṃ sudhanvā nādhirohati ||
english: Are brahmins better, Virochana, or the sons of Diti? And why does Sudhanva not sit on the couch?

speaker: Virochana
devanagari:
तथा भद्रे करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे ।
सुधन्वानं च मां चैव प्रातर्द्रष्टासि सङ्गतौ ॥
iast:
tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase |
sudhanvānaṃ ca māṃ caiva prātardraṣṭāsi saṅgatau ||
english: I will do as you say, gentle and timid one. In the morning you will see Sudhanva and me together.

speaker: Sudhanva
devanagari:
अन्वालभे हिरण्मयं प्राह्रादेऽहं तवासनम् ।
एकत्वमुपसम्पन्नो न त्वासेयं त्वया सह ॥
iast:
anvālabhe hiraṇmayaṃ prāhrāde'haṃ tavāsanam |
ekatvamupasampanno na tvāseyaṃ tvayā saha ||
english: I touch your golden seat, son of Prahlada, but I have not come to equality with you; I will not sit with you.
codex_problem: The English incorrectly negates “coming into equality”; the Sanskrit instead makes equal or shared seating the circumstance Sudhanva rejects.
codex_sanskrit_says: I touch your golden seat, son of Prahlada, but I would not sit with you on equal terms.

speaker: Sudhanva
devanagari:
पितापि ते समासीनमुपासीतैव मामधः ।
बालः सुखैधितो गेहे न त्वं किं चन बुध्यसे ॥
iast:
pitāpi te samāsīnamupāsītaiva māmadhaḥ |
bālaḥ sukhaidhito gehe na tvaṃ kiṃ cana budhyase ||
english: Even your father would sit below me when I sit as an equal. You are a child, raised in comfort at home; you understand nothing.
codex_problem: “When I sit as an equal” is not in the Sanskrit and obscures Sudhanva's assertion of superior rank.
codex_sanskrit_says: Even your father would attend upon me from below while I was seated. You are a child raised comfortably at home and understand nothing.

speaker: Sudhanva
devanagari:
हिरण्यं च गवाश्वं च तवैवास्तु विरोचन ।
प्राणयोस्तु पणं कृत्वा प्रश्नं पृच्छाव ये विदुः ॥
iast:
hiraṇyaṃ ca gavāśvaṃ ca tavaivāstu virocana |
prāṇayostu paṇaṃ kṛtvā praśnaṃ pṛcchāva ye viduḥ ||
english: Keep your gold, cows and horses, Virochana. Let us stake our lives instead, and put the question to those who know.

speaker: Sudhanva
devanagari:
पञ्च पश्वनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते ।
शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते ॥
iast:
pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte |
śatamaśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte ||
english: A lie about cattle destroys five; a lie about cows destroys ten; a lie about horses destroys a hundred; a lie about people destroys a thousand.
codex_problem: Paśu means an animal or livestock generally, not specifically cattle; rendering it as “cattle” collapses the distinction from the cows named next.
codex_sanskrit_says: A lie concerning an animal destroys five; one concerning a cow destroys ten, one concerning a horse a hundred, and one concerning a person a thousand.

speaker: Prahlada
devanagari:
मत्तः श्रेयानङ्गिरा वै सुधन्वा त्वद्विरोचन ।
मातास्य श्रेयसी मातुस्तस्मात्त्वं तेन वै जितः ॥
iast:
mattaḥ śreyānaṅgirā vai sudhanvā tvadvirocana |
mātāsya śreyasī mātustasmāttvaṃ tena vai jitaḥ ||
english: Angiras is better than I am, and Sudhanva is better than you, Virochana. His mother is better than your mother; so you have been defeated by him.

speaker: Prahlada
devanagari:
विरोचन सुधन्वायं प्राणानामीश्वरस्तव ।
सुधन्वन्पुनरिच्छामि त्वया दत्तं विरोचनम् ॥
iast:
virocana sudhanvāyaṃ prāṇānāmīśvarastava |
sudhanvanpunaricchāmi tvayā dattaṃ virocanam ||
english: Virochana, this Sudhanva is now master of your life. Sudhanva, I would have Virochana given back to me by you.

speaker: Sudhanva
devanagari:
यद्धर्ममवृणीथास्त्वं न कामादनृतं वदीः ।
पुनर्ददामि ते तस्मात्पुत्रं प्रह्राद दुर्लभम् ॥
iast:
yaddharmamavṛṇīthāstvaṃ na kāmādanṛtaṃ vadīḥ |
punardadāmi te tasmātputraṃ prahrāda durlabham ||
english: Because you chose dharma and did not speak falsely out of desire, I give you back your son, Prahlada, so hard to find again.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न छन्दांसि वृजिनात्तारयन्ति
आयाविनं मायया वर्तमानम् ।
नीडं शकुन्ता इव जातपक्षाश्
छन्दांस्येनं प्रजहत्यन्तकाले ॥
iast:
na chandāṃsi vṛjināttārayanti
āyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam |
nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś
chandāṃsyenaṃ prajahatyantakāle ||
english: The Vedic verses do not carry across sin a deceitful person who lives by deceit; at the end they leave him, as fledged birds leave the nest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सामुद्रिकं वणिजं चोरपूर्वं
शलाक धूर्तं च चिकित्सकं च ।
अरिं च मित्रं च कुशीलवं च
नैतान्साख्येष्वधिकुर्वीत सप्त ॥
iast:
sāmudrikaṃ vaṇijaṃ corapūrvaṃ
śalāka dhūrtaṃ ca cikitsakaṃ ca |
ariṃ ca mitraṃ ca kuśīlavaṃ ca
naitānsākhyeṣvadhikurvīta sapta ||
english: A palm-reader, a merchant who was once a thief, a gambler, a physician, an enemy, a friend and a performer: these seven should not be made witnesses.
codex_problem: The English divides and combines the opening terms incorrectly. Sāmudrikaṃ vaṇijam is a sea-going merchant, while corapūrvam is a separate former thief; the verse does not say “a palm-reader” and “a merchant who was once a thief.”
codex_sanskrit_says: A sea-going merchant, a former thief, a gambler, a physician, an enemy, a friend and a performer—these seven should not be appointed as witnesses.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अगार दाही गरदः कुण्डाशी सोमविक्रयी ।
पर्व कारश्च सूची च मित्र ध्रुक्पारदारिकः ॥
iast:
agāra dāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī |
parva kāraśca sūcī ca mitra dhrukpāradārikaḥ ||
english: One who sets houses on fire, a poisoner, one who lives off an adulteress's son, a seller of soma, a maker of arrows, an astrologer, one who betrays a friend, an adulterer,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
भ्रूणहा गुरु तल्पी च यश्च स्यात्पानपो द्विजः ।
अतितीक्ष्णश्च काकश्च नास्तिको वेद निन्दकः ॥
iast:
bhrūṇahā guru talpī ca yaśca syātpānapo dvijaḥ |
atitīkṣṇaśca kākaśca nāstiko veda nindakaḥ ||
english: one who kills an embryo, one who violates his teacher's bed, a twice-born who drinks, one who is excessively harsh, a crow-like person, an unbeliever, a reviler of the Veda,

why_listed: Codex disagrees; safety flags: caste_gender; random sample
speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्रुव प्रग्रहणो व्रात्यः कीनाशश्चार्थवानपि ।
रक्षेत्युक्तश्च यो हिंस्यात्सर्वे ब्रह्मण्हणैः समाः ॥
iast:
sruva pragrahaṇo vrātyaḥ kīnāśaścārthavānapi |
rakṣetyuktaśca yo hiṃsyātsarve brahmaṇhaṇaiḥ samāḥ ||
english: one who takes up the ladle though outcaste, a peasant even when wealthy, and one who harms someone who asked for protection: all these are equal to killers of brahmins.
codex_problem: The English combines “one who takes up the sacrificial ladle” and “a vrātya” into one person, although the Sanskrit lists them separately.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who takes up the sacrificial ladle, a vrātya, a peasant even if wealthy, and one who harms a person who has appealed for protection are all equal to killers of brahmins.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तृणोक्लया ज्ञायते जातरूपं
युगे भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः ।
शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः
कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश् च ॥
iast:
tṛṇoklayā jñāyate jātarūpaṃ
yuge bhadro vyavahāreṇa sādhuḥ |
śūro bhayeṣvarthakṛcchreṣu dhīraḥ
kṛcchrāsvāpatsu suhṛdaścārayaś ca ||
english: Gold is known by a flame of grass, the good by their dealings, the virtuous by their conduct, the brave in times of fear, the steady in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times and calamities.
codex_problem: The English omits the image of a good draught animal being proved in the yoke and replaces it with two generalized tests of good and virtuous people.
codex_sanskrit_says: Gold is known by a flame of grass, a good draught animal in the yoke, and an honest person by dealings; the brave are known amid dangers, the steadfast in financial distress, and friends and enemies in hardships and calamities.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा
मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया ।
क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्य सेवा
ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः ॥
iast:
jarā rūpaṃ harati hi dhairyamāśā
mṛtyuḥ prāṇāndharmacaryāmasūyā |
krodhaḥ śriyaṃ śīlamanārya sevā
hriyaṃ kāmaḥ sarvamevābhimānaḥ ||
english: Old age robs beauty, hope robs patience, death robs life, envy robs the practice of dharma, anger robs good fortune, serving the ignoble robs good character, lust robs modesty, and pride robs everything.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सत्यं रूपं श्रुतं विद्या कौल्यं शीलं बलं धनम् ।
शौर्यं च चिरभाष्यं च दशः संसर्गयोनयः ॥
iast:
satyaṃ rūpaṃ śrutaṃ vidyā kaulyaṃ śīlaṃ balaṃ dhanam |
śauryaṃ ca cirabhāṣyaṃ ca daśaḥ saṃsargayonayaḥ ||
english: Truth, beauty, learning, knowledge, family, character, strength, wealth, courage and varied speech: these ten are the sources of association.
codex_problem: “Varied speech” does not translate cirabhāṣyam; that would require a reading such as citrabhāṣyam.
codex_sanskrit_says: The tenth item is cirabhāṣyam, meaning long or prolonged speech.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
असूयको दन्द शूको निष्ठुरो वैरकृन्नरः ।
स कृच्छ्रं महदाप्नोतो नचिरात्पापमाचरन् ॥
iast:
asūyako danda śūko niṣṭhuro vairakṛnnaraḥ |
sa kṛcchraṃ mahadāpnoto nacirātpāpamācaran ||
english: The envious, the biting, the harsh and the one who makes enemies, doing wrong, soon meets great trouble.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रज्ञामेवागमयति यः प्राज्ञेभ्यः स पण्डितः ।
प्राज्ञो ह्यवाप्य धर्मार्थौ शक्नोति सुखमेधितुम् ॥
iast:
prajñāmevāgamayati yaḥ prājñebhyaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ |
prājño hyavāpya dharmārthau śaknoti sukhamedhitum ||
english: One who gains wisdom from the wise is truly wise; for the wise, having gained dharma and true benefit, can grow in happiness.
codex_problem: “True benefit” adds “true” and obscures artha, while “grow in happiness” changes the construction sukham edhitum.
codex_sanskrit_says: The wise person, having obtained dharma and artha, can prosper happily.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धसुखं वसेत् ।
यावज्जीवेन तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत् ॥
iast:
pūrve vayasi tatkuryādyena vṛddhasukhaṃ vaset |
yāvajjīvena tatkuryādyena pretya sukhaṃ vaset ||
english: In youth one should do what lets one live happily in old age, and throughout life what lets one live happily after death.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
जीर्णमन्नं प्रशंसन्ति भार्यं च गतयौवनाम् ।
शूरं विगतसङ्ग्रामं गतपारं तपस्विनम् ॥
iast:
jīrṇamannaṃ praśaṃsanti bhāryaṃ ca gatayauvanām |
śūraṃ vigatasaṅgrāmaṃ gatapāraṃ tapasvinam ||
english: They praise food once digested, a wife whose youth has passed, a hero whose battles are over, and an ascetic who has reached the far shore.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ऋषीणां च नदीनां च कुलानां च महामनाम् ।
प्रभवो नाधिगन्तव्यः स्त्रीणां दुश्चरितस्य च ॥
iast:
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca kulānāṃ ca mahāmanām |
prabhavo nādhigantavyaḥ strīṇāṃ duścaritasya ca ||
english: The origin of sages, of rivers, of great-souled families, and of women's misconduct should not be investigated.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्विजातिपूजाभिरतो दाता ज्ञातिषु चार्जवी ।
क्षत्रियः स्वर्गभाग्राजंश्चिरं पालयते महीम् ॥
iast:
dvijātipūjābhirato dātā jñātiṣu cārjavī |
kṣatriyaḥ svargabhāgrājaṃściraṃ pālayate mahīm ||
english: A kshatriya devoted to honouring the twice-born, generous and straightforward with his kin, rules the earth long, king, and gains heaven.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
बुद्धिश्रेष्ठानि कर्माणि बाहुमध्यानि भारत ।
तानि जङ्घा जघन्यानि भारप्रत्यवराणि च ॥
iast:
buddhiśreṣṭhāni karmāṇi bāhumadhyāni bhārata |
tāni jaṅghā jaghanyāni bhārapratyavarāṇi ca ||
english: Deeds of the intellect are best, Bharata; deeds of the arms are middling; deeds of the legs are lowest, and carrying loads lower still.

speaker: the Sadhyas
devanagari:
साध्या देवा वय्मस्मो महर्षे
दृष्ट्वा भवन्तं न शक्नुमोऽनुमातुम् ।
श्रुतेन धीरो बुद्धिमांस्त्वं मतो नः
काव्यां वाचं वक्तुमर्हस्युदाराम् ॥
iast:
sādhyā devā vaymasmo maharṣe
dṛṣṭvā bhavantaṃ na śaknumo'numātum |
śrutena dhīro buddhimāṃstvaṃ mato naḥ
kāvyāṃ vācaṃ vaktumarhasyudārām ||
english: We are the Sadhya gods, great sage. Seeing you, we cannot fathom you. You are known to us as steady and wise through learning; please speak noble, wise words.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश् चोपसेवते ।
यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥
iast:
yādṛśaiḥ saṃvivadate yādṛśāṃś copasevate |
yādṛgicchecca bhavituṃ tādṛgbhavati pūruṣaḥ ||
english: Such as those he quarrels with, such as those he serves, and such as he wishes to be: such a person becomes.
codex_problem: Saṃvivadate means conversing or associating with people, not quarrelling with them.
codex_sanskrit_says: A person becomes like those with whom he converses, those whom he serves, and what he wishes to become.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
यतो यतो निवर्तते ततस्ततो विमुच्यते ।
निवर्तनाद्धि सर्वतो न वेत्ति दुःखमण्वपि ॥
iast:
yato yato nivartate tatastato vimucyate |
nivartanāddhi sarvato na vetti duḥkhamaṇvapi ||
english: From whatever one turns away, from that one is freed. By turning away from everything, one does not know even the slightest pain.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
दुःशासनस्तूपहन्ता न शास्ता
नावर्तते मन्युवशात्कृतघ्नः ।
न कस्य चिन्मित्रमथो दुरात्मा
कलाश्चैता अधमस्येह पुंसः ॥
iast:
duḥśāsanastūpahantā na śāstā
nāvartate manyuvaśātkṛtaghnaḥ |
na kasya cinmitramatho durātmā
kalāścaitā adhamasyeha puṃsaḥ ||
english: Harsh in command, a destroyer rather than a guide, not turning back from anger, ungrateful, friend to no one, evil-minded: these are the marks of the lowest person here.
codex_problem: “Harsh in command” reverses the sense of duḥśāsana, which describes someone difficult to govern, restrain, or instruct.
codex_sanskrit_says: The lowest person is difficult to govern or instruct, an injurer rather than a guide, unrelenting under anger, ungrateful, friendless, and evil-minded.

speaker: the swan
devanagari:
न श्रद्दधाति कल्याणं परेभ्योऽप्यात्मशङ्कितः ।
निराकरोति मित्राणि यो वै सोऽधम पूरुषः ॥
iast:
na śraddadhāti kalyāṇaṃ parebhyo'pyātmaśaṅkitaḥ |
nirākaroti mitrāṇi yo vai so'dhama pūruṣaḥ ||
english: One who, doubting himself, does not believe any good of others, and drives away his friends, is the lowest person.
codex_problem: “Does not believe any good of others” changes the direction of parebhyaḥ: the person distrusts what is good or beneficial when it comes from others, rather than disbelieving that others possess goodness.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who, being suspicious, does not trust what is beneficial from others and drives away friends is the lowest person.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
महाकुलानां स्पृहयन्ति देवा
धर्मार्थवृद्धाश्च बहुश्रुताश् च ।
पृच्छामि त्वां विदुर प्रश्नमेतं
भवन्ति वै कानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
mahākulānāṃ spṛhayanti devā
dharmārthavṛddhāśca bahuśrutāś ca |
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vidura praśnametaṃ
bhavanti vai kāni mahākulāni ||
english: The gods, those grown in dharma and true benefit, and the deeply learned admire great families. I ask you this question, Vidura: which families are truly great?
codex_problem: Spṛhayanti means “desire” or “long for,” not merely “admire,” and artha is replaced by the interpretive phrase “true benefit.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The gods, those advanced in dharma and artha, and the deeply learned long for great families; Dhritarashtra asks which families are great.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तमो दमो ब्रह्मवित्त्वं वितानाः
पुण्या विवाहाः सततान्न दानम् ।
येष्वेवैते सप्तगुणा भवन्ति
सम्यग्वृत्तास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
tamo damo brahmavittvaṃ vitānāḥ
puṇyā vivāhāḥ satatānna dānam |
yeṣvevaite saptaguṇā bhavanti
samyagvṛttāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Austerity, self-control, knowledge of the Veda, sacrifices, pure marriages and constant giving of food: families in which these seven qualities are found and practised rightly are great families.
codex_problem: As supplied, the Sanskrit begins tamo, “darkness,” not tapo, “austerity”; the English silently translates the likely intended emendation rather than the given text.
codex_sanskrit_says: As written, it begins “darkness, self-control, knowledge of Brahman/the Veda, sacrifices, pure marriages, and constant giving of food”; tapo would instead mean “austerity.”

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येषां न वृत्तं व्यथते न योनिर्
वृत्तप्रसादेन चरन्ति धर्मम् ।
ये कीर्तिमिच्छन्ति कुले विशिष्टां
त्यक्तानृतास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
yeṣāṃ na vṛttaṃ vyathate na yonir
vṛttaprasādena caranti dharmam |
ye kīrtimicchanti kule viśiṣṭāṃ
tyaktānṛtāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Those whose conduct does not falter, who do not shame their ancestry, who practise dharma with a glad heart, who wish for distinguished fame for their family and have given up falsehood: those are great families.
codex_problem: Vṛttaprasādena refers to the purity or excellence of conduct, not to practising dharma “with a glad heart.”
codex_sanskrit_says: They practise dharma through the purity or excellence of their conduct, seek distinguished family renown, and have abandoned falsehood.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनिज्ययाविवाहैर्श्च वेदस्योत्सादनेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
anijyayāvivāhairśca vedasyotsādanena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti dharmasyātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through neglecting sacrifice, through improper marriages, through abandoning the Veda, and through transgressing dharma, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
देव द्रव्यविनाशेन ब्रह्म स्वहरणेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
deva dravyavināśena brahma svaharaṇena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through destroying what belongs to the gods, stealing brahmins' property, and slighting brahmins, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणानां परिभवात्परिवादाच्च भारत ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति न्यासापहरणेन च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavātparivādācca bhārata |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti nyāsāpaharaṇena ca ||
english: Through contempt for brahmins and slander of them, Bharata, and through stealing deposits held in trust, families fall to low standing.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
मा नः कुले वैरकृत्कश् चिदस्तु
राजामात्यो मा परस्वापहारी ।
मित्रद्रोही नैकृतिकोऽनृती वा
पूर्वाशी वा पितृदेवातिथिभ्यः ॥
iast:
mā naḥ kule vairakṛtkaś cidastu
rājāmātyo mā parasvāpahārī |
mitradrohī naikṛtiko'nṛtī vā
pūrvāśī vā pitṛdevātithibhyaḥ ||
english: May there be none in our family who makes enmity, no king's minister who steals others' property, no betrayer of friends, no deceiver or liar, and none who eats before the ancestors, gods and guests.
codex_problem: The English incorrectly makes “king’s minister” modify the person who steals. The Sanskrit lists a king’s minister and a thief of others’ property as separate unwanted members of the family.
codex_sanskrit_says: May our family contain no maker of enmity, king’s minister, thief of another’s property, betrayer of friends, deceiver, liar, or person who eats before the ancestors, gods, and guests.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्च नो ब्राह्मणं हन्याद्यश्च नो ब्राह्मणान्द्विषेत् ।
न नः स समितिं गच्छेद्यश्च नो निर्वपेत्कृषिम् ॥
iast:
yaśca no brāhmaṇaṃ hanyādyaśca no brāhmaṇāndviṣet |
na naḥ sa samitiṃ gacchedyaśca no nirvapetkṛṣim ||
english: Whoever among us kills a brahmin or hates brahmins, and whoever among us takes up farming, let him not come to our assembly.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सूक्ष्मोऽपि भारं नृपते स्यन्दनो वै
शक्तो वोढुं न तथान्ये महीजाः ।
एवं युक्ता भारसहा भवन्ति
महाकुलीना न तथान्ये मनुष्याः ॥
iast:
sūkṣmo'pi bhāraṃ nṛpate syandano vai
śakto voḍhuṃ na tathānye mahījāḥ |
evaṃ yuktā bhārasahā bhavanti
mahākulīnā na tathānye manuṣyāḥ ||
english: Even a small chariot, king, can bear a load that other things from the earth cannot. So people of great families, when joined to a task, bear the burden, and other people do not.
codex_problem: Mahījāḥ here means trees or earth-born wood, not the much broader “things from the earth.”
codex_sanskrit_says: Even a small chariot can bear a burden, whereas other trees or pieces of wood cannot; similarly, people of great families can bear burdens that others cannot.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सत्कृताश्च कृतार्थाश्च मित्राणां न भवन्ति ये ।
तान्मृतानपि क्रव्यादाः कृतघ्नान्नोपभुञ्जते ॥
iast:
satkṛtāśca kṛtārthāśca mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye |
tānmṛtānapi kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnānnopabhuñjate ||
english: Those who, honoured and helped by friends, do not stand by them: even flesh-eating creatures will not eat such ungrateful people when dead.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थयेदेव मित्राणि सति वासति वा धने ।
नानर्थयन्विजानाति मित्राणां सारफल्गुताम् ॥
iast:
arthayedeva mitrāṇi sati vāsati vā dhane |
nānarthayanvijānāti mitrāṇāṃ sāraphalgutām ||
english: One should seek out friends whether one has wealth or not; without asking of them, one does not learn which friends are solid and which hollow.
codex_problem: Arthayet means to ask or make a request of friends, not simply to “seek out” friends.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should make requests of friends whether wealth is present or absent; without asking them, one cannot discover which friends are substantial and which are hollow.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पुनर्नरो म्रियते जायते च
पुनर्नरो हीयते वर्धते पुनः ।
पुनर्नरो याचति याच्यते च
पुनर्नरः शोचति शोच्यते पुनः ॥
iast:
punarnaro mriyate jāyate ca
punarnaro hīyate vardhate punaḥ |
punarnaro yācati yācyate ca
punarnaraḥ śocati śocyate punaḥ ||
english: Again and again a person dies and is born; again and again a person declines and grows; again and again a person begs and is begged from; again and again a person grieves and is grieved for.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च
लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च ।
पर्यायशः सर्वमिह स्पृशन्ति
तस्माद्धीरो नैव हृष्येन्न शोचेत् ॥
iast:
sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavau ca
lābhālābhau maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca |
paryāyaśaḥ sarvamiha spṛśanti
tasmāddhīro naiva hṛṣyenna śocet ||
english: Pleasure and pain, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: all these touch everyone in turn. So the steady person neither exults nor grieves.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
तनुरुच्छः शिखी राजा मिथ्योपचरितो मया ।
मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति ॥
iast:
tanurucchaḥ śikhī rājā mithyopacarito mayā |
mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ yuddhenāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
english: King Yudhishthira, like a slender flame, whom I treated falsely, will put an end to my foolish sons in war.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
बुद्ध्या भयं प्रणुदति तपसा विन्दते महत् ।
गुरुशुश्रूषया ज्ञानं शान्तिं त्यागेन विन्दति ॥
iast:
buddhyā bhayaṃ praṇudati tapasā vindate mahat |
guruśuśrūṣayā jñānaṃ śāntiṃ tyāgena vindati ||
english: By understanding one drives away fear; by austerity one gains greatness; by serving the teacher one gains knowledge; by letting go one finds peace.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनाश्रिता दानपुण्यं वेद पुण्यमनाश्रिताः ।
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ता विचरन्तीह मोक्षिणः ॥
iast:
anāśritā dānapuṇyaṃ veda puṇyamanāśritāḥ |
rāgadveṣavinirmuktā vicarantīha mokṣiṇaḥ ||
english: Not depending on the merit of giving, not depending on the merit of the Veda, free of attraction and aversion, those who seek liberation move about here.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्वधीतस्य सुयुद्धस्य सुकृतस्य च कर्मणः ।
तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य तस्यान्ते सुखमेधते ॥
iast:
svadhītasya suyuddhasya sukṛtasya ca karmaṇaḥ |
tapasaśca sutaptasya tasyānte sukhamedhate ||
english: At the end of well-done study, a well-fought battle, a good deed and well-practised austerity, happiness grows.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सम्भाव्यं गोषु सम्पन्नं सम्भाव्यं ब्राह्मणे तपः ।
सम्भाव्यं स्त्रीषु चापल्यं सम्भाव्यं ज्ञातितो भयम् ॥
iast:
sambhāvyaṃ goṣu sampannaṃ sambhāvyaṃ brāhmaṇe tapaḥ |
sambhāvyaṃ strīṣu cāpalyaṃ sambhāvyaṃ jñātito bhayam ||
english: Wealth is to be expected in cows, austerity in a brahmin, fickleness in women, and danger from kin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणेषु च ये शूराः स्त्रीषु ज्ञातिषु गोषु च ।
वृन्तादिव फलं पक्वं धृतराष्ट्र पतन्ति ते ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca ye śūrāḥ strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca |
vṛntādiva phalaṃ pakvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra patanti te ||
english: Those who show their courage against brahmins, women, kin and cows fall, Dhritarashtra, like ripe fruit from the stalk.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अवध्या ब्राह्मणा गावो स्त्रियो बालाश्च ज्ञातयः ।
येषां चान्नानि भुञ्जीत ये च स्युः शरणागताः ॥
iast:
avadhyā brāhmaṇā gāvo striyo bālāśca jñātayaḥ |
yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ ||
english: Not to be killed are brahmins, cows, women, children, kinsmen, those whose food one has eaten, and those who come for refuge.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न मनुष्ये गुणः कश्चिदन्यो धनवताम् अपि ।
अनातुरत्वाद्भद्रं ते मृतकल्पा हि रोगिणः ॥
iast:
na manuṣye guṇaḥ kaścidanyo dhanavatām api |
anāturatvādbhadraṃ te mṛtakalpā hi rogiṇaḥ ||
english: No other quality in a person, even the wealthy, matters like freedom from illness, bless you; the sick are as good as dead.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पुरा ह्युक्तो नाकरोस्त्वं वचो मे
द्यूते जितां द्रौपदीं प्रेक्ष्य राजन् ।
दुर्योधनं वारयेत्यक्षवत्यां
कितवत्वं पण्डिता वर्जयन्ति ॥
iast:
purā hyukto nākarostvaṃ vaco me
dyūte jitāṃ draupadīṃ prekṣya rājan |
duryodhanaṃ vārayetyakṣavatyāṃ
kitavatvaṃ paṇḍitā varjayanti ||
english: Earlier, seeing Draupadi won at the dice game, I told you, king, 'Stop Duryodhana'; you did not follow my words. The wise avoid gambling.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्राः पाण्डवान्पालयन्तु
पाण्डोः सुतास्तव पुत्रांश्च पान्तु ।
एकारिमित्राः कुरवो ह्येकमन्त्रा
जीवन्तु राजन्सुखिनः समृद्धाः ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ pāṇḍavānpālayantu
pāṇḍoḥ sutāstava putrāṃśca pāntu |
ekārimitrāḥ kuravo hyekamantrā
jīvantu rājansukhinaḥ samṛddhāḥ ||
english: Let Dhritarashtra's sons protect the Pandavas, and let Pandu's sons protect your sons. Let the Kurus, with one enemy and one friend and one counsel, live happy and prosperous, king.
codex_problem: “One enemy and one friend” wrongly treats eka as numerical; the compound describes the Kurus as sharing the same friends and enemies.
codex_sanskrit_says: Let the Kurus, having common friends and enemies and united in counsel, live happy and prosperous, O king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सन्धत्स्व त्वं कौरवान्पाण्डुपुत्रैर्
मा तेऽन्तरं रिपवः प्रार्थयन्तु ।
सत्ये स्थितास्ते नरदेव सर्वे
दुर्योधनं स्थापय त्वं नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
sandhatsva tvaṃ kauravānpāṇḍuputrair
mā te'ntaraṃ ripavaḥ prārthayantu |
satye sthitāste naradeva sarve
duryodhanaṃ sthāpaya tvaṃ narendra ||
english: Make peace between the Kauravas and the sons of Pandu; do not let enemies look for a gap between you. They all stand in truth, god among men; restrain Duryodhana, lord of men.
codex_problem: “A gap between you” changes te antaram, which means an opening or vulnerable point belonging to the king, not necessarily a division between the two parties.
codex_sanskrit_says: Do not let your enemies seek an opening or weakness in you.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सप्तदशेमान्राजेन्द्र मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत् ।
वैचित्रवीर्य पुरुषानाकाशं मुष्टिभिर्घ्नतः ॥
iast:
saptadaśemānrājendra manuḥ svāyambhuvo'bravīt |
vaicitravīrya puruṣānākāśaṃ muṣṭibhirghnataḥ ||
english: Svayambhuva Manu, lord of kings, spoke of these seventeen people, son of Vichitravirya, who strike the sky with their fists,
codex_problem: The English incorrectly makes “lord of kings” an epithet of Manu; rā́jendra is a vocative addressed to Dhritarashtra.
codex_sanskrit_says: O lord of kings, O son of Vichitravirya, Svayambhuva Manu spoke of these seventeen men who strike the sky with their fists.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्चाशिष्यं शासति यश् च कुप्यते
यश्चातिवेलं भजते द्विषन्तम् ।
स्त्रियश्च योऽरक्षति भद्रमस्तु ते
यश्चायाच्यं याचति यश् च कत्थते ॥
iast:
yaścāśiṣyaṃ śāsati yaś ca kupyate
yaścātivelaṃ bhajate dviṣantam |
striyaśca yo'rakṣati bhadramastu te
yaścāyācyaṃ yācati yaś ca katthate ||
english: one who instructs the unteachable, one who gets angry, one who serves an enemy beyond measure, one who does not protect women, bless you, one who begs what should not be begged, and one who boasts;
codex_problem: The English reverses yo ’rakṣati: this is ā-rakṣati, “guards” or “tries to guard,” not “does not protect.”
codex_sanskrit_says: The list includes one who tries to guard or control women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वध्वा हासं श्वशुरो यश् च मन्यते
वध्वा वसन्नुत यो मानकामः ।
परक्षेत्रे निर्वपति यश्च बीजं
स्त्रियं च यः परिवदतेऽतिवेलम् ॥
iast:
vadhvā hāsaṃ śvaśuro yaś ca manyate
vadhvā vasannuta yo mānakāmaḥ |
parakṣetre nirvapati yaśca bījaṃ
striyaṃ ca yaḥ parivadate'tivelam ||
english: a father-in-law who jokes with his daughter-in-law, one who lives with his daughter-in-law and wants honour, one who sows seed in another's field, and one who speaks ill of women beyond measure;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् ।
एतानि मानवान्घ्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते ॥
iast:
eta evāsayastīkṣṇāḥ kṛntantyāyūṃṣi dehinām |
etāni mānavānghnanti na mṛtyurbhadramastu te ||
english: These are the sharp swords that cut short the lives of embodied beings. These kill people, not death; bless you.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विश्वस्तस्यैति यो दारान्यश्चापि गुरु तक्पगः ।
वृषली पतिर्द्विजो यश्च पानपश्चैव भारत ॥
iast:
viśvastasyaiti yo dārānyaścāpi guru takpagaḥ |
vṛṣalī patirdvijo yaśca pānapaścaiva bhārata ||
english: One who goes to the wife of a man who trusts him, one who violates his teacher's bed, a twice-born man who marries a shudra woman, and a drinker, Bharata,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
शरणागतहा चैव सर्वे ब्रह्महणैः समाः ।
एतैः समेत्य कर्तव्यं प्रायश्चित्तमिति श्रुतिः ॥
iast:
śaraṇāgatahā caiva sarve brahmahaṇaiḥ samāḥ |
etaiḥ sametya kartavyaṃ prāyaścittamiti śrutiḥ ||
english: and one who kills a refugee: all are equal to killers of brahmins. Scripture says that having fallen in with these, one must do atonement.
codex_problem: “Refugee” is too broad and modern for śaraṇāgata, which specifically denotes someone who has come seeking refuge or protection.
codex_sanskrit_says: The list includes one who kills a person who has sought refuge or protection.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान्रक्षेद्धनैरपि ।
आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि ॥
iast:
āpadarthaṃ dhanaṃ rakṣeddārānrakṣeddhanairapi |
ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣeddārairapi dhanairapi ||
english: One should guard wealth against misfortune; guard one's wife even with wealth; and always guard oneself, even with wife and wealth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उक्तं मया द्यूतकालेऽपि राजन्
नैवं युक्तं वचनं प्रातिपीय ।
तदौषधं पथ्यमिवातुरस्य
न रोचते तव वैचित्र वीर्य ॥
iast:
uktaṃ mayā dyūtakāle'pi rājan
naivaṃ yuktaṃ vacanaṃ prātipīya |
tadauṣadhaṃ pathyamivāturasya
na rocate tava vaicitra vīrya ||
english: I said at the time of the dice game, king, that this was not right. But like medicine to a sick man, that beneficial advice did not please you, son of Vichitravirya.
codex_problem: The English omits the vocative prātipīya, “descendant of Pratipa.”
codex_sanskrit_says: I said at the time of the dice game, O king, O descendant of Pratipa, that this was not right; that advice did not please you, O son of Vichitravirya, just as beneficial medicine does not please a sick man.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अस्तब्धमक्लीबमदीर्घसूत्रं
सानुक्रोशं श्लक्ष्णमहार्यमन्यैः ।
अरोग जातीयमुदारवाक्यं
दूतं वदन्त्यष्ट गुणोपपन्नम् ॥
iast:
astabdhamaklībamadīrghasūtraṃ
sānukrośaṃ ślakṣṇamahāryamanyaiḥ |
aroga jātīyamudāravākyaṃ
dūtaṃ vadantyaṣṭa guṇopapannam ||
english: Not stubborn, not timid, not slow, compassionate, gentle, not to be won over by others, of healthy stock and eloquent: they call such an envoy endowed with eight qualities.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न निह्नवं सत्र गतस्य गच्छेत्
संसृष्ट मन्त्रस्य कुसङ्गतस्य ।
न च ब्रूयान्नाश्वसामि त्वयीति
स कारणं व्यपदेशं तु कुर्यात् ॥
iast:
na nihnavaṃ satra gatasya gacchet
saṃsṛṣṭa mantrasya kusaṅgatasya |
na ca brūyānnāśvasāmi tvayīti
sa kāraṇaṃ vyapadeśaṃ tu kuryāt ||
english: One should not contradict a man sitting in an assembly whose counsel is mixed with bad company; nor should one say 'I do not trust you', but should give a reason or excuse.
codex_problem: The first half is misconstrued: nihnavam means concealment or denial, while saṃsṛṣṭamantrasya refers to someone with whom counsel or secrets have been shared, not to counsel being “mixed with bad company.”
codex_sanskrit_says: One should not resort to concealment or denial concerning one who has gone to the assembly, with whom counsel has been shared, and who has fallen into bad company; one should not say “I do not trust you,” but should give a reason or pretext.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
घृणी राजा पुंश्चली राजभृत्यः
पुत्रो भ्राता विधवा बाल पुत्रा ।
सेना जीवी चोद्धृत भक्त एव
व्यवहारे वै वर्जनीयाः स्युरेते ॥
iast:
ghṛṇī rājā puṃścalī rājabhṛtyaḥ
putro bhrātā vidhavā bāla putrā |
senā jīvī coddhṛta bhakta eva
vyavahāre vai varjanīyāḥ syurete ||
english: A compassionate king, a loose woman, a king's servant, a son, a brother, a widow with a young son, one who lives by soldiering, and one who has lost his position: these should be avoided in transactions.
codex_problem: Uddhṛtabhakta does not simply mean someone who has lost his position; it denotes someone whose food, ration, or maintenance has been withdrawn.
codex_sanskrit_says: A compassionate king, a loose woman, a royal servant, a son, a brother, a widow with a young son, a soldier, and one whose maintenance has been withdrawn should be avoided in transactions.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गुणा दश स्नानशीलं भजन्ते
बलं रूपं स्वरवर्णप्रशुद्धिः ।
स्पर्शश्च गन्धश्च विशुद्धता च
श्रीः सौकुमार्यं प्रवराश्च नार्यः ॥
iast:
guṇā daśa snānaśīlaṃ bhajante
balaṃ rūpaṃ svaravarṇapraśuddhiḥ |
sparśaśca gandhaśca viśuddhatā ca
śrīḥ saukumāryaṃ pravarāśca nāryaḥ ||
english: Ten benefits come to one who bathes regularly: strength, beauty, a clear voice and complexion, softness of touch, fragrance, purity, fortune, delicacy, and the finest women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कदर्यमाक्रोशकमश्रुतं च
वराक सम्भूतममान्य मानिनम् ।
निष्ठूरिणं कृतवैरं कृतघ्नम्
एतान्भृतार्तोऽपि न जातु याचेत् ॥
iast:
kadaryamākrośakamaśrutaṃ ca
varāka sambhūtamamānya māninam |
niṣṭhūriṇaṃ kṛtavairaṃ kṛtaghnam
etānbhṛtārto'pi na jātu yācet ||
english: A miser, an abuser, the unlearned, the base-born who honours the dishonourable, the harsh, one who has made enemies, and the ungrateful: one should never beg from these, even in distress.
codex_problem: Amānyamāninam does not mean someone who honours the dishonourable; it means someone who thinks highly of himself despite being unworthy of honour. The base-born person and this conceited person are also separate items in the list.
codex_sanskrit_says: One should never beg, even in distress, from a miser, an abuser, an unlearned person, one of base origin, one who considers himself worthy of honour although he is not, a harsh person, one who has made enemies, or an ingrate.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सहायबन्धना ह्यर्थाः सहायाश्चार्थबन्धनाः ।
अन्योन्यबन्धनावेतौ विनान्योन्यं न सिध्यतः ॥
iast:
sahāyabandhanā hyarthāḥ sahāyāścārthabandhanāḥ |
anyonyabandhanāvetau vinānyonyaṃ na sidhyataḥ ||
english: Aims are bound to helpers, and helpers are bound to means; these two are bound to each other, and neither succeeds without the other.
codex_problem: The English renders the repeated artha as two different things, “aims” and “means,” obscuring the verse’s stated mutual dependence between only two parties.
codex_sanskrit_says: Resources or undertakings depend upon helpers, and helpers depend upon resources; the two depend upon each other, and neither succeeds without the other.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उत्पाद्य पुत्राननृणांश्च कृत्वा
वृत्तिं च तेभ्योऽनुविधाय कां चित् ।
स्थाने कुमारीः प्रतिपाद्य सर्वा
अरण्यसंस्थो मुनिवद्बुभूषेत् ॥
iast:
utpādya putrānanṛṇāṃśca kṛtvā
vṛttiṃ ca tebhyo'nuvidhāya kāṃ cit |
sthāne kumārīḥ pratipādya sarvā
araṇyasaṃstho munivadbubhūṣet ||
english: Having fathered sons and freed them from debt, having arranged some livelihood for them, and having given all daughters in marriage properly, one should wish to live in the forest as a sage.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हितं यत्सर्वभूतानामात्मनश्च सुखावहम् ।
तत्कुर्यादीश्वरो ह्येतन्मूलं धर्मार्थसिद्धये ॥
iast:
hitaṃ yatsarvabhūtānāmātmanaśca sukhāvaham |
tatkuryādīśvaro hyetanmūlaṃ dharmārthasiddhaye ||
english: What is beneficial to all beings and brings happiness to oneself, the lord should do; this is the root of success in dharma and true benefit.
codex_problem: “True benefit” adds an unsupported qualification and does not accurately preserve artha, the second term paired with dharma.
codex_sanskrit_says: The lord should do what benefits all beings and brings happiness to himself, for this is the root of attaining dharma and artha, or material welfare.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पश्य दोषान्पाण्डवैर्विग्रहे त्वं
यत्र व्यथेरन्नपि देवाः स शक्राः ।
पुत्रैर्वैरं नित्यमुद्विग्नवासो
यशः प्रणाशो द्विषतां च हर्षः ॥
iast:
paśya doṣānpāṇḍavairvigrahe tvaṃ
yatra vyatherannapi devāḥ sa śakrāḥ |
putrairvairaṃ nityamudvignavāso
yaśaḥ praṇāśo dviṣatāṃ ca harṣaḥ ||
english: See the evils in a conflict with the Pandavas, at which even the gods with Indra would tremble: enmity with your sons, living in constant anxiety, loss of fame and the joy of enemies.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
भीष्मस्य कोपस्तव चेन्द्र कल्प
द्रोणस्य राज्ञश्च युधिष्ठिरस्य ।
उत्सादयेल्लोकमिमं प्रवृद्धः
श्वेतो ग्रहस्तिर्यगिवापतन्खे ॥
iast:
bhīṣmasya kopastava cendra kalpa
droṇasya rājñaśca yudhiṣṭhirasya |
utsādayellokamimaṃ pravṛddhaḥ
śveto grahastiryagivāpatankhe ||
english: The anger of Bhishma, of you who are like Indra, of Drona and of King Yudhishthira, once roused, could destroy this world, like a white comet falling across the sky.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्रा वनं राजन्व्याघ्राः पाण्डुसुता मताः ।
मा वनं छिन्धि स व्याघ्रं मा व्याघ्रान्नीनशो वनात् ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrā vanaṃ rājanvyāghrāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ |
mā vanaṃ chindhi sa vyāghraṃ mā vyāghrānnīnaśo vanāt ||
english: Dhritarashtra's sons are a forest, king, and Pandu's sons are held to be the tigers. Do not cut down the forest with its tigers; do not drive the tigers out of the forest.
codex_problem: The second imperative uses a form of naś, “perish” or “destroy”; “drive the tigers out” softens this to mere expulsion.
codex_sanskrit_says: Dhritarashtra’s sons are the forest and Pandu’s sons the tigers. Do not cut down the forest together with its tigers, and do not destroy or cause the tigers to perish from the forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येन त्वेतानि सर्वाणि सङ्गृहीतानि भारत ।
यद्बलानां बलं श्रेष्ठं तत्प्रज्ञा बलमुच्यते ॥
iast:
yena tvetāni sarvāṇi saṅgṛhītāni bhārata |
yadbalānāṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tatprajñā balamucyate ||
english: But the strength by which all these are gathered together, Bharata, the best of all strengths, is called the strength of wisdom.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्त्रीषु राजसु सर्पेषु स्वाध्याये शत्रुसेविषु ।
भोगे चायुषि विश्वासं कः प्राज्ञः कर्तुमर्हति ॥
iast:
strīṣu rājasu sarpeṣu svādhyāye śatruseviṣu |
bhoge cāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ kaḥ prājñaḥ kartumarhati ||
english: In women, kings and snakes, in one's own learning, in those who serve the enemy, in enjoyment and in life itself: what wise person would place trust?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति ।
प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान्पतिपद्यते ॥
iast:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati |
pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpatipadyate ||
english: The life-breaths of a young person rise up when an elder approaches; by rising and greeting him, he regains them.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चिकित्सकः शक्य कर्तावकीर्णी
स्तेनः क्रूरो मद्यपो भ्रूणहा च ।
सेनाजीवी श्रुतिविक्रायकश् च
भृशं प्रियोऽप्यतिथिर्नोदकार्हः ॥
iast:
cikitsakaḥ śakya kartāvakīrṇī
stenaḥ krūro madyapo bhrūṇahā ca |
senājīvī śrutivikrāyakaś ca
bhṛśaṃ priyo'pyatithirnodakārhaḥ ||
english: A physician, a surgeon, one who has broken his vow of celibacy, a thief, a cruel person, a drinker, one who kills embryos, one who lives by soldiering, and one who sells the Veda: however dear, such a guest is not worthy of water.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अरोषणो यः समलोष्ट काञ्चनः
प्रहीण शोको गतसन्धि विग्रहः ।
निन्दा प्रशंसोपरतः प्रियाप्रिये
चरन्नुदासीनवदेष भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
aroṣaṇo yaḥ samaloṣṭa kāñcanaḥ
prahīṇa śoko gatasandhi vigrahaḥ |
nindā praśaṃsoparataḥ priyāpriye
carannudāsīnavadeṣa bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: One who is free of anger, to whom a clod and gold are the same, who has left grief behind, is beyond alliance and conflict, has stopped caring for blame and praise, and moves among the pleasant and unpleasant as if indifferent: this is a mendicant.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नीवार मूलेङ्गुद शाकवृत्तिः
सुसंयतात्माग्निकार्येष्वचोद्यः ।
वने वसन्नतिथिष्वप्रमत्तो
धुरन्धरः पुण्यकृदेष तापसः ॥
iast:
nīvāra mūleṅguda śākavṛttiḥ
susaṃyatātmāgnikāryeṣvacodyaḥ |
vane vasannatithiṣvapramatto
dhurandharaḥ puṇyakṛdeṣa tāpasaḥ ||
english: Living on wild rice, roots, ingudi nuts and greens, well self-controlled, needing no urging in the fire rites, living in the forest and attentive to guests: this foremost doer of good is an ascetic.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनीर्ष्युर्गुप्तदारः स्यात्संविभागी प्रियंवदः ।
श्लक्ष्णो मधुरवाक्स्त्रीणां न चासां वशगो भवेत् ॥
iast:
anīrṣyurguptadāraḥ syātsaṃvibhāgī priyaṃvadaḥ |
ślakṣṇo madhuravākstrīṇāṃ na cāsāṃ vaśago bhavet ||
english: One should be free of jealousy, guard one's wife, share with others, speak kindly, be gentle and sweet-spoken to women, but not come under their control.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पूजनीया महाभागाः पुण्याश्च गृहदीप्तयः ।
स्त्रियः श्रियो गृहस्योक्तास्तस्माद्रक्ष्या विशेषतः ॥
iast:
pūjanīyā mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāśca gṛhadīptayaḥ |
striyaḥ śriyo gṛhasyoktāstasmādrakṣyā viśeṣataḥ ||
english: Women are worthy of honour, greatly blessed, pure and the light of the house. They are called the fortune of the home; so they should be protected above all.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पितुरन्तःपुरं दद्यान्मातुर्दद्यान्महानसम् ।
गोषु चात्मसमं दद्यात्स्वयमेव कृषिं व्रजेत् ।
भृत्यैर्वणिज्याचारं च पुत्रैः सेवेत ब्राह्मणान् ॥
iast:
piturantaḥpuraṃ dadyānmāturdadyānmahānasam |
goṣu cātmasamaṃ dadyātsvayameva kṛṣiṃ vrajet |
bhṛtyairvaṇijyācāraṃ ca putraiḥ seveta brāhmaṇān ||
english: Give the inner apartments to your father, give the kitchen to your mother, give the cattle to one like yourself, and go to the farming yourself. Carry on trade through servants, and serve brahmins through your sons.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम् ।
तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति ॥
iast:
adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam |
teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati ||
english: Fire arose from water, the kshatriya from the brahmin, iron from stone. Their power reaches everywhere, but it is quenched in its own source.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नासुहृत्परमं मन्त्रं भारतार्हति वेदितुम् ।
अपण्डितो वापि सुहृत्पण्डितो वाप्यनात्मवान् ।
अमात्ये ह्यर्थलिप्सा च मन्त्ररक्षणमेव च ॥
iast:
nāsuhṛtparamaṃ mantraṃ bhāratārhati veditum |
apaṇḍito vāpi suhṛtpaṇḍito vāpyanātmavān |
amātye hyarthalipsā ca mantrarakṣaṇameva ca ||
english: One who is not a friend does not deserve to know one's highest counsel, Bharata; nor does a friend who is unwise, nor a wise one who lacks self-control. Choose a minister only after testing him, for on him depend gaining wealth and keeping counsel.
codex_problem: “Choose a minister only after testing him” is an addition not present in the Sanskrit.
codex_sanskrit_says: An enemy, an unwise friend, and a wise but uncontrolled person are unfit to know the highest counsel; the acquisition of wealth and the safeguarding of counsel depend upon a minister.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अमोघक्रोधहर्षस्य स्वयं कृत्यान्ववेक्षिणः ।
आत्मप्रत्यय कोशस्य वसुधेयं वसुन्धरा ॥
iast:
amoghakrodhaharṣasya svayaṃ kṛtyānvavekṣiṇaḥ |
ātmapratyaya kośasya vasudheyaṃ vasundharā ||
english: For one whose anger and joy are not fruitless, who personally oversees what must be done, and whose treasury is known to himself, this earth yields wealth.
codex_problem: The final clause turns a statement of possession or dominion into the different claim that the earth “yields wealth.”
codex_sanskrit_says: This wealth-bearing earth belongs to the person whose anger and pleasure are effective, who personally oversees what must be done, and who has personal command or assured knowledge of his treasury.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणं वेद भर्ता वेद स्त्रियं तथा ।
अमात्यं नृपतिर्वेद राजा राजानमेव च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaṃ veda bhartā veda striyaṃ tathā |
amātyaṃ nṛpatirveda rājā rājānameva ca ||
english: A brahmin knows a brahmin, a husband knows his wife, a king knows his minister, and a king knows a king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न शत्रुरङ्कमापन्नो मोक्तव्यो वध्यतां गतः ।
अहताद्धि भयं तस्माज्जायते नचिरादिव ॥
iast:
na śatruraṅkamāpanno moktavyo vadhyatāṃ gataḥ |
ahatāddhi bhayaṃ tasmājjāyate nacirādiva ||
english: An enemy who has fallen into one's lap and deserves death should not be let go; for danger soon arises from one who is not killed.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रसादो निष्फलो यस्य क्रोधश्चापि निरर्थकः ।
न तं भर्तारमिच्छन्ति षण्ढं पतिमिव स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
prasādo niṣphalo yasya krodhaścāpi nirarthakaḥ |
na taṃ bhartāramicchanti ṣaṇḍhaṃ patimiva striyaḥ ||
english: One whose favour bears no fruit and whose anger is also without effect: people do not want him as master, as women do not want an impotent husband.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येऽर्थाः स्त्रीषु समासक्ताः प्रथमोत्पतितेषु च ।
ये चानार्य समासक्ताः सर्वे ते संशयं गताः ॥
iast:
ye'rthāḥ strīṣu samāsaktāḥ prathamotpatiteṣu ca |
ye cānārya samāsaktāḥ sarve te saṃśayaṃ gatāḥ ||
english: Wealth entrusted to women, to those newly risen, and to the ignoble: all of it falls into doubt.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्र स्त्री यत्र कितवो यत्र बालोऽनुशास्ति च ।
मज्जन्ति तेऽवशा देशा नद्यामश्मप्लवा इव ॥
iast:
yatra strī yatra kitavo yatra bālo'nuśāsti ca |
majjanti te'vaśā deśā nadyāmaśmaplavā iva ||
english: Where a woman, a gambler or a child gives the orders, those lands sink helplessly, like a raft of stone in a river.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यं प्रशंसन्ति कितवा यं प्रशंसन्ति चारणाः ।
यं प्रशंसन्ति बन्धक्यो न स जीवति मानवः ॥
iast:
yaṃ praśaṃsanti kitavā yaṃ praśaṃsanti cāraṇāḥ |
yaṃ praśaṃsanti bandhakyo na sa jīvati mānavaḥ ||
english: The man whom gamblers praise, whom bards praise, whom loose women praise: that man does not truly live.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हित्वा तान्परमेष्वासान्पाण्डवानमितौजसः ।
आहितं भारतैश्वर्यं त्वया दुर्योधने महत् ॥
iast:
hitvā tānparameṣvāsānpāṇḍavānamitaujasaḥ |
āhitaṃ bhārataiśvaryaṃ tvayā duryodhane mahat ||
english: Abandoning the Pandavas, great archers of boundless energy, you have placed the great sovereignty of the Bharatas in Duryodhana, Bharata.
codex_problem: The final vocative “Bharata” is an addition. The verse's only form of that word is part of the compound meaning “the sovereignty of the Bharatas,” which the English has already translated.
codex_sanskrit_says: Abandoning the Pandavas, supreme archers of boundless energy, you have placed the great sovereignty of the Bharatas in Duryodhana.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
अनीश्वरोऽयं पुरुषो भवाभवे
सूत्रप्रोता दारुमयीव योषा ।
धात्रा हि दिष्टस्य वशे किलायं
तस्माद्वद त्वं श्रवणे घृतोऽहम् ॥
iast:
anīśvaro'yaṃ puruṣo bhavābhave
sūtraprotā dārumayīva yoṣā |
dhātrā hi diṣṭasya vaśe kilāyaṃ
tasmādvada tvaṃ śravaṇe ghṛto'ham ||
english: This person is not master of his rising or falling; he is like a wooden doll moved by strings. He is under the control of what the Creator has ordained. So speak on; I am intent on listening.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रियो भवति दानेन प्रियवादेन चापरः ।
मन्त्रं मूलबलेनान्यो यः प्रियः प्रिय एव सः ॥
iast:
priyo bhavati dānena priyavādena cāparaḥ |
mantraṃ mūlabalenānyo yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ ||
english: One becomes dear through gifts, another through pleasant words, another through the strength of counsel and charms; but one who is dear is dear simply.
codex_problem: “Counsel and charms” misreads mantra and mūla in this context: they refer to incantations and roots or herbs used for their magical power.
codex_sanskrit_says: One becomes dear through gifts, another through pleasant speech, and another through the power of incantations and roots; but one who is naturally dear remains dear.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
सर्वं त्वमायती युक्तं भाषसे प्राज्ञसंमतम् ।
न चोत्सहे सुतं त्यक्तुं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः ॥
iast:
sarvaṃ tvamāyatī yuktaṃ bhāṣase prājñasaṃmatam |
na cotsahe sutaṃ tyaktuṃ yato dharmastato jayaḥ ||
english: All that you say is sound for the future and approved by the wise. Yet I cannot bring myself to abandon my son. Where dharma is, there is victory.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ये पापा इति विख्याताः संवासे परिगर्हिताः ।
युक्ताश्चान्यैर्महादोषैर्ये नरास्तान्विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
ye pāpā iti vikhyātāḥ saṃvāse parigarhitāḥ |
yuktāścānyairmahādoṣairye narāstānvivarjayet ||
english: Those known to be wicked, censured by those who live with them, and joined to other great faults: one should avoid such people.
codex_problem: “Censured by those who live with them” assigns the censure to cohabitants. The Sanskrit says that association or living with such people is itself condemned.
codex_sanskrit_says: Those known as wicked, whose company is condemned, and who possess other great faults should be avoided.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
श्रीमन्तं ज्ञातिमासाद्य यो ज्ञातिरवसीदति ।
दिग्धहस्तं मृग इव स एनस्तस्य विन्दति ॥
iast:
śrīmantaṃ jñātimāsādya yo jñātiravasīdati |
digdhahastaṃ mṛga iva sa enastasya vindati ||
english: If a relative comes to a prosperous relative and still suffers, the prosperous one incurs his sin, as a hunter with a poisoned arrow incurs the deer's.
codex_problem: The English reverses who acquires whose sin and attaches the simile incorrectly. Grammatically, the suffering relative is the subject of both avasīdati and vindati.
codex_sanskrit_says: A relative who, after approaching a prosperous relative, still sinks into distress acquires that prosperous relative’s sin, like a deer approaching someone whose hand is smeared with poison.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अपनीतं सुनीतेन योऽर्थं प्रत्यानिनीषते ।
मतिमास्थाय सुदृढां तदकापुरुष व्रतम् ॥
iast:
apanītaṃ sunītena yo'rthaṃ pratyāninīṣate |
matimāsthāya sudṛḍhāṃ tadakāpuruṣa vratam ||
english: One who, holding to a firm resolve, seeks by good conduct to win back a gain lost through bad conduct: that is the vow of a person who is no coward.
codex_problem: The English adds that the gain was lost “through bad conduct.” The Sanskrit does not state what caused the loss; apanītam means that the wealth or objective was taken away or lost.
codex_sanskrit_says: One who, adopting a very firm resolve, seeks to recover by sound policy what has been taken away or lost follows the vow of one who is no coward.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
दुःखार्तेषु प्रमत्तेषु नास्तिकेष्वलसेषु च ।
न श्रीर्वसत्यदान्तेषु ये चोत्साह विवर्जिताः ॥
iast:
duḥkhārteṣu pramatteṣu nāstikeṣvalaseṣu ca |
na śrīrvasatyadānteṣu ye cotsāha vivarjitāḥ ||
english: Fortune does not dwell with those overcome by sorrow, the careless, unbelievers, the lazy, the undisciplined, and those without energy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अग्निहोत्रफला वेदाः शीलवृत्तफलं श्रुतम् ।
रतिपुत्र फला दारा दत्तभुक्त फलं धनम् ॥
iast:
agnihotraphalā vedāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam |
ratiputra phalā dārā dattabhukta phalaṃ dhanam ||
english: The fruit of the Vedas is the fire offering; the fruit of learning is good character and conduct; the fruit of a wife is love and sons; the fruit of wealth is giving and enjoying it.
codex_problem: “Love” softens and changes rati, which here denotes sexual pleasure or intercourse.
codex_sanskrit_says: The fruit of a wife is sexual pleasure and sons.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उत्थानं संयमो दाक्ष्यमप्रमादो धृतिः स्मृतिः ।
समीक्ष्य च समारम्भो विद्धि मूलं भवस्य तत् ॥
iast:
utthānaṃ saṃyamo dākṣyamapramādo dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ |
samīkṣya ca samārambho viddhi mūlaṃ bhavasya tat ||
english: Effort, self-restraint, skill, attentiveness, steadiness, memory, and starting things after careful thought: know these as the root of prosperity.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्त्री धूर्तकेऽलसे भीरौ चण्डे पुरुषमानिनि ।
चौरे कृतघ्ने विश्वासो न कार्यो न च नास्तिके ॥
iast:
strī dhūrtake'lase bhīrau caṇḍe puruṣamānini |
caure kṛtaghne viśvāso na kāryo na ca nāstike ||
english: Trust should not be placed in a woman, a cheat, a lazy person, a coward, a fierce person, one who boasts of his manliness, a thief, an ungrateful person, or an unbeliever.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविद्यः पुरुषः शोच्यः शोच्यं मिथुनमप्रजम् ।
निराहाराः प्रजाः शोच्याः शोच्यं राष्ट्रमराजकम् ॥
iast:
avidyaḥ puruṣaḥ śocyaḥ śocyaṃ mithunamaprajam |
nirāhārāḥ prajāḥ śocyāḥ śocyaṃ rāṣṭramarājakam ||
english: An uneducated person is to be pitied; a couple without children is to be pitied; people without food are to be pitied; a kingdom without a king is to be pitied.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अध्वा जरा देहवतां पर्वतानां जलं जरा ।
असम्भोगो जरा स्त्रीणां वाक्षल्यं मनसो जरा ॥
iast:
adhvā jarā dehavatāṃ parvatānāṃ jalaṃ jarā |
asambhogo jarā strīṇāṃ vākṣalyaṃ manaso jarā ||
english: Travel is old age for embodied beings; water is old age for mountains; lack of enjoyment is old age for women; harsh words are old age for the mind.
codex_problem: “Lack of enjoyment” obscures the specifically sexual sense of asambhoga in this context.
codex_sanskrit_says: Lack of sexual union or intercourse is old age for women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनाम्नाय मला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम् ।
कौतूहलमला साध्वी विप्रवास मलाः स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
anāmnāya malā vedā brāhmaṇasyāvrataṃ malam |
kautūhalamalā sādhvī vipravāsa malāḥ striyaḥ ||
english: Not reciting is the stain of the Vedas; not keeping vows is the stain of a brahmin; curiosity is the stain of a virtuous woman; living away from home is the stain of women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न स्वप्नेन जयेन्निद्रां न कामेन स्त्रियं जयेत् ।
नेन्धनेन जयेदग्निं न पानेन सुरां जयेत् ॥
iast:
na svapnena jayennidrāṃ na kāmena striyaṃ jayet |
nendhanena jayedagniṃ na pānena surāṃ jayet ||
english: One cannot conquer sleep by sleeping, nor a woman by desire, nor fire by fuel, nor liquor by drinking.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्य दानजितं मित्रममित्रा युधि निर्जिताः ।
अन्नपानजिता दाराः सफलं तस्य जीवितम् ॥
iast:
yasya dānajitaṃ mitramamitrā yudhi nirjitāḥ |
annapānajitā dārāḥ saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam ||
english: One whose friends are won by gifts, whose enemies are conquered in battle, and whose wives are won by food and drink: his life is fruitful.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहि यवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः ।
नालमेकस्य तत्सर्वमिति पश्यन्न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
yatpṛthivyāṃ vrīhi yavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ |
nālamekasya tatsarvamiti paśyanna muhyati ||
english: All the rice, barley, gold, cattle and women on earth are not enough for even one person: one who sees this is not deluded.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः ।
नान्तकः सर्वभूतानां न पुंसां वामलोचना ॥
iast:
nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ |
nāntakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanā ||
english: Fire is never satisfied with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers, nor death with all beings, nor a beautiful-eyed woman with men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आशा धृतिं हन्ति समृद्धिमन्तकः
क्रोधः श्रियं हन्ति यशः कदर्यता ।
अपालनं हन्ति पशूंश्च राजन्न्
एकः क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणो हन्ति राष्ट्रम् ॥
iast:
āśā dhṛtiṃ hanti samṛddhimantakaḥ
krodhaḥ śriyaṃ hanti yaśaḥ kadaryatā |
apālanaṃ hanti paśūṃśca rājann
ekaḥ kruddho brāhmaṇo hanti rāṣṭram ||
english: Craving destroys steadiness; death destroys prosperity; anger destroys fortune; miserliness destroys fame; neglect destroys cattle, king; and one angry brahmin destroys a kingdom.
codex_problem: Āśā means hope, expectation, or longing; rendering it as “craving” narrows and reinterprets the statement.
codex_sanskrit_says: Hope or expectation destroys steadfastness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अजश्च कांस्यं च रथश्च नित्यं
मध्वाकर्षः शकुनिः श्रोत्रियश् च ।
वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नो वयस्य
एतानि ते सन्तु गृहे सदैव ॥
iast:
ajaśca kāṃsyaṃ ca rathaśca nityaṃ
madhvākarṣaḥ śakuniḥ śrotriyaś ca |
vṛddho jñātiravasanno vayasya
etāni te santu gṛhe sadaiva ||
english: Goats, bronze, a chariot, honey, a bird, a Vedic scholar, an aged relative and a friend fallen on hard times: may these always be in your house.
codex_problem: The English incorrectly separates madhvākarṣaḥ śakuniḥ into “honey” and “a bird.” It is a single expression describing a honey-drawing or honey-attracting bird.
codex_sanskrit_says: The list includes a honey-drawing bird, not honey and a bird as separate items.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अजोक्षा चन्दनं वीणा आदर्शो मधुसर्पिषी ।
विषमौदुम्बरं शङ्खः स्वर्णं नाभिश्च रोचना ॥
iast:
ajokṣā candanaṃ vīṇā ādarśo madhusarpiṣī |
viṣamaudumbaraṃ śaṅkhaḥ svarṇaṃ nābhiśca rocanā ||
english: A goat and a bull, sandalwood, a lute, a mirror, honey and ghee, poison-curing fig wood, a conch, gold, musk and yellow pigment:
codex_problem: The English combines viṣam and audumbaram into the unsupported compound “poison-curing fig wood,” adding a curing relationship that the Sanskrit does not state.
codex_sanskrit_says: The verse separately lists poison and an object made of udumbara (fig) wood.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
महाबलान्पश्य मनानुभावान्
प्रशास्य भूमिं धनधान्य पूर्णाम् ।
राज्यानि हित्वा विपुलांश्च भोगान्
गतान्नरेन्द्रान्वशमन्तकस्य ॥
iast:
mahābalānpaśya manānubhāvān
praśāsya bhūmiṃ dhanadhānya pūrṇām |
rājyāni hitvā vipulāṃśca bhogān
gatānnarendrānvaśamantakasya ||
english: See the mighty and great-souled kings who ruled the earth, full of wealth and grain, and then, leaving their kingdoms and vast enjoyments, went under the power of death.
